en: Flow on, O Soma, with your sweetest and most intoxicating stream,
pressed for Indra to drink. The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, flows toward his place, the one that bestows vigor.
He has taken his seat upon the wooden vessel.
Be the bestower of the widest space, the most generous, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra;
bring across the bounty of the liberal patrons.
Flow toward the banquet of the great gods with your exhilarating juice;
flow toward booty and fame.
We approach you for this very purpose, day after day.
O Indu, our hopes are placed in you.
The Daughter of the Sun purifies your Soma as it flows around,
through the eternal fleece of the sheep’s wool.
Him, the slender ones, the ten sisters, the maidens, seize together at the gathering on the decisive day.
The agile ones urge him forward; they blow the leather bag like a bellows.
The honey is a threefold protection. And the inviolable cows, the milch-cows, mix this child with their milk—
the Soma for Indra to drink.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], Indra slays all the Vṛtras;
as a hero, he bestows riches upon us.
Flow forth, O Soma, for the sake of the gods, through the filter with speed.
O Indu, as a bull, enter Indra. Flow hither, O Indu, as great food, most resplendent, O bull.
As a sustainer, sit upon your seat.

They have milked the beloved honey, the streams of the pressed juice of the wise ordainer; the one of good intent has clothed himself in the waters. The great rivers flow along after you, the great one.
When you clothe yourself in the rays of light;
the ocean has been purified among the waters, the support and sustainer of heaven— Soma, seeking us, flows through the filter.
The tawny bull has bellowed; great and fair to behold like Mitra, he shines together with the sun.
O Indu, the active songs are being polished for you with power.
With those [streams] by which you adorn yourself for exhilaration— We pray to you, the maker of wide space, for that exhilaration, O impetuous one; Great indeed are your praises.
O Indu, seeking Indra, flow for us with a stream of honey,
like Parjanya rich in rain.
O Indu, win cattle, win men, win horses, and win booty.
The ancient soul of the sacrifice;
this immortal god flies like a bird toward the wooden vats to sit within them.
This god, purified by the fingers, rushes across the obstacles; he is Pavamāna, the invincible.
This god, while being purified, is extolled by those who desire the Truth.
The tawny one is cleansed for the sake of booty;
this Pavamāna, like a hero going forth with his warriors, seeks to win all desirable things.
This god speeds on his chariot; as he flows clear, he bestows gifts.
He makes his voice manifest. Praised by the sages, this god plunges into the waters.
Bestowing jewels upon the donor,
he rushes through the mid-air regions toward heaven with his stream,
bellowing as he flows clear.
He has spread across the sky, passing through the regions untouched, Pavamāna, the one who makes the sacrifice perfect. By his ancient birth, this god, pressed for the gods, [flows on].
The tawny one flows through the filter.
This very one, of many vows, being born, engendering nourishments, flows in a stream, pressed out.
Win, O Soma, and conquer, O Pavamāna, great renown;
and then make us more prosperous. Win the light, win the sun, and all felicities, O Soma.
And so...
O Soma, from of old, drive away skill and will as well; strike down our adversaries.
And so...
O purifiers, purify the Soma for Indra to drink;
then...
Do thou grant us a share in the sun through thy wisdom and thy protections.
RV_09.004.06.1: By your wisdom and by your aids, may we long behold the sun.
Flow toward us, O Soma, well-armed one, with doubly-mighty wealth;
and then...
Flow toward us, O unshakable one, as a conqueror in battles, bringing wealth.
Then...
RV_09.004.09.1 {23} They have magnified thee with sacrifices, O Pavamāna, in the supporting firmament;
O Indu, bring us wondrous wealth that sustains all people, together with the Ashvins.
And then... Enkindled, the Lord of all, Pavamāna shines forth on every side.
Gladdening, the bull, bellowing loudly—
Tanūnapāt, the purifying one, flows while sharpening his horns, shining brightly through the mid-air.
Worthy of praise, Pavamāna shines forth as resplendent wealth; with his might, he flows with streams of honey.
Spreading the sacrificial grass eastward with his power, the tawny Pavamāna shines.
The god moves among the gods;
the golden, divine doors rise up on high,
well-praised by Pavamāna.
Pavamāna yearns for the two great, vast, and well-fashioned ones,
Night and Dawn, who are beautiful to behold. I invoke both the divine Hotṛ-priests, the gods who watch over men.
Pavamāna is Indra, the bull. Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, and the great Īḷā— may these three goddesses, beautifully adorned, come to this sacrifice of ours as Pavamāna flows.
I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the first-born guardian who goes before;
Indu is Indra, the bull, the golden-hued Pavamāna, the Lord of Creatures.
O Pavamāna, anoint the Lord of the Forest with a stream of honeyed juice.
Thousand-branched, green, radiant, and golden— O All-Gods, come to the *svāhā*-utterance of Pavamāna;
may Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra be of one accord.
O Soma, flow with a pleasant stream as a bull, seeking the gods; flow through the sheep’s wool, longing for us.
O Indu, pour forth that exhilarating intoxication toward Indra.
Toward the prize-winning steeds;
toward that ancient exhilarating draught, flow, being pressed, into the filter,
toward strength and fame.
The drops, the Soma juices, have flowed along like waters down a slope;
being purified, they have reached Indra.
The ten young women cleanse him, as one cleanses a prize-winning steed.
Mix together for the sake of the sacrifice and for exhilaration the pressed juice, that vigorous essence, like a bull playing in the forest beyond the sheep-fence.
The god, pressed for the god Indra, flows forth, sustaining him;
as his milk swells, he flows. The soul of the sacrifice, being pressed with speed, flows forth as the libation.
He guards the ancient wisdom of the seers.
Thus, O most intoxicating one, being purified and longing for Indra, flow for his enjoyment;
even though you are hidden in secret, you hold fast to our songs.

The drops have been poured forth along the path according to the law of cosmic order, they who possess great splendor, knowing the course of this [sacrifice]. The foremost stream of honeyed juice plunges into the mighty waters.
The oblation among oblations, worthy of praise;
the foremost bull has bellowed toward the woods, releasing his joined voices—
the true sacrifice proceeding toward the seats.
When the sage, clothing himself in poetic wisdom and manly powers, flows around,
the prize-winning steed desires to win the light of heaven.
As he purifies himself, he sits like a king over the rival clans.
When the wise ones set him in motion,
the beloved tawny one sits within the sheep’s wool and the wooden vessels; as a singer,
he is implored with hymns.
He goes together with Vāyu, Indra, and the Aśvins, along with the exhilarating juice, he who delights according to his laws.
The waves of the sweet mead flow toward Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga.
Knowing this through his powers,
O Heaven and Earth, win for us wealth, sweetness, and the acquisition of strength;
conquer glory and riches.
These Soma juices have flowed forth toward the beloved desire of Indra, increasing his heroic power. Being purified, seated in the bowls, they go toward Vāyu and the Aśvins.
May they bestow upon us great heroic strength.
O Soma, as you are being purified for the sake of Indra’s bounty, stir his heart;
sit upon the seat of the *ṛta*.
The ten fingers cleanse you; the seven prayers impel you. The sages have rejoiced after you.
For the sake of the gods and for exhilaration, they release you through the sheep’s fleece.
We clothe him with the milk of cows. Being purified in the jars, the ruddy, golden-hued one has clothed himself in garments made of milk.
Flow for us from the bountiful one; strike away all our enemies.
O Indu, enter as a friend.
Flow down the rain from heaven; flow forth splendor from the earth.
O Soma, grant us victory in battles.
May we partake of you, who look upon men, who are drunk by Indra, and who find the light of heaven— granting us progeny and nourishment.
The sage of heaven, the beloved one, having been established among the daughters, goes forth being pressed— bestowing vital strengths, he whose wisdom is that of a seer.
Onward and onward he goes for the sake of the praiseworthy dwelling, pleasing to the people who are free from guile.
Flow for our enjoyment with your most delightful [stream].
He, the pure son, as soon as he was born, caused his two parents to shine;
Great, he has illumined the two great ones who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).

Urged on by the seven prayers, he has quickened the guileless rivers, which have magnified his single eye. They have established him, the youthful one, as the unconquered conqueror for the sake of greatness.
The drop, O Indra, is within your service.
The immortal bearer, speeding along, beholds the seven;
Krivī has satisfied the goddesses.
Help us in our ritual arrangements, O Hero; O Soma, fight away the darknesses. Purifying yourself, you have struck them down. Now, for each newer and newer hymn, prepare the paths.
As of old, cause the lights to shine.
O Pavamāna, bestow great renown, cattle, horses, and heroic sons;
win wisdom and win the light of heaven.
Like chariots that have been urged forward, like coursers seeking renown,
the Soma drops have flowed forth for the sake of wealth.
Urged onward like chariots, they have sped from the hands [of the priests].
They bear [the prize] like the singers of hymns;
the Soma-drops, like kings, are anointed with praises and with milk,
as a sacrifice is prepared by the seven ordainers.
The drops, being pressed for exhilaration with great power and song, flow forth in a stream once they have been poured.
Having drunk from Vivasvat, they bring forth the light of the dawn.
The heroes spread out the fine [woof].
The ancient singers open the doors of hymns for the impetuous might of the Bull. The Āyus [approach] him.
The seven co-born Hotṛ-priests sit together, facing one another; they fill out the station of the One.
I have joined my kinship with your kinship, even as the eye is united with the sun.
The offspring of the poet yields [the milk]. [He beholds] the dear station of heaven, hidden in the cave by the Adhvaryu priests;
the Sun beholds it with his eye.
Sing forth, O men, for this Indu as he flows clear;
he seeks to reach the gods. The Atharvans have mixed milk with your honeyed juice.
O God, for the sake of the God-loving one, [purify yourself].
Flow for us, bringing well-being to our cattle, well-being to our people, and well-being to our horses; O King, bring well-being to the plants.
Sing a song for Soma, the tawny one, who is self-strong, ruddy, and touches the heavens.
Purify the pressed Soma with stones set in motion by the hands.
In the sweet juice, pour forth the sweetness! Sit down with reverence; mix it with curd!
Place the Soma-drop within Indra.
O Soma, slayer of enemies, most active among men, flow clear for the welfare of our cattle;
acting according to the will of the gods,
flow for Indra to drink and for his exhilaration.
RV 9.11.8.2: O you who are built of mind, lord of the mind!
RV 9.11.9.1: O Soma Pavamāna, bestow upon us wealth consisting of heroic power.
RV 9.11.9.2: O Indu, together with Indra as our ally!
The Soma drops have been poured forth, the pressed juices at the seat of Ṛta,
most rich in sweetness for Indra. The inspired singers have shouted toward him, as mother cows low toward their calf.
Indra [is summoned] for the drinking of the Soma. Distilling exhilaration, the wise Soma dwells in his seat upon the wave of the river, resting upon the *gaurī*.
Far-sighted at the navel of heaven,
Soma, the wise seer of noble power, is magnified within the fleece of the sheep.
That Soma which has been placed within the jars, set inside the filter.
Indu has embraced him. Indu sends forth his voice upon the summit of the ocean, enlivening the honey-dripping reservoir.
The Lord of the Forest, whose praise is eternal, the end of prayers, yielding abundance within;
impelling the human generations,
Soma flows toward the beloved stations of heaven as he is urged forth.
The sage [flows] with the stream of the inspired poet.
O Pavamāna, bestow upon us wealth of a thousandfold luster, O Indu, that which is self-sustaining.
Soma, being purified, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool,
to the appointed place of Vāyu and Indra. O you who seek aid, sing forth to the purifying Sage.
Pressed for the feast of the gods,
the Soma juices, possessing thousandfold power, flow clear for the winning of booty,
being praised for the feast of the gods.
And flow for us, for the winning of booty, with great nourishments;
O Indu, [grant] resplendent and heroic strength.
May they flow for us with thousandfold wealth and heroic strength.
The divine drops, being pressed,
have been released like steeds urged on by their drivers, for the winning of the prize;
the swift ones have passed through the sheep’s wool filter.
The lowing drops flow like milch-cows toward their calf;
they have run forth from the two arms.
O Pavamāna, bellowing loudly, you flow as a gladdening draught, dear to Indra.
Strike down all enemies;
O purifying ones, who behold the light of heaven, driving away the stingy niggards,
sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
The sage has flowed all around, resting upon the wave of the river;
bearing the much-desired song of praise, when the five kindred tribes, active in their work, [sing] with their voice.
They adorn the steadfast one;
all the gods have become exhilarated by the juice of this impetuous one,
when he clothes himself in milk.
Stripping away his body, he runs forth, casting off the arrow-heads; there he strikes together with his companion.
He who, like a bright youth, has been cleansed by the daughters of Vivasvat.
Making the cows his own garment, he goes beyond the two transverse paths seeking cattle through the narrow openings;
he utters the sound which he has found.
The swift fingers have gathered together, purifying the lord of nourishment;
they grasp the back of the vigorous steed. O Soma, you encompass all things celestial and terrestrial.
Come seeking us, bringing treasures.
By means of subtle wisdom, this hero goes with swift chariots,
proceeding to the appointed place of Indra.
He meditates extensively with his thought upon the great assembly of the gods,
where the immortals dwell.
He, being well-placed, is led forth along the path frequented by the radiant ones.
When the impetuous ones strike him down,
this bull of the herd, shaking his horns, whets them; he assumes manly powers by his might.
This vigorous one moves along with golden ornaments and brilliant rays,
becoming the lord of the rivers.
Having gone across with his rugged, solid form, he has surpassed all treasures.
He goes down into the filters;
the men cleanse him who is worthy of cleansing within the wooden vats,
as he prepares great nourishments.
RV 9.15.8: Him, the well-armed and most intoxicating one, the ten fingers and the seven prayers cleanse. RV 9.16.1: O pressers, pour forth his juice from the vessel for the sake of wild exhilaration.
Like a released steed,
Etaśa has sped forth; with wisdom, we follow him who is the charioteer of skill, who clothes himself in the waters with his juice, the winner of cattle among the small [grains].
Release the Soma, which is unassailable even in the waters and difficult to cross, into the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink.
With a mindful spirit, the Soma flows through the filter as it is being purified.
Through his wisdom, he has taken his seat in the assembly place.
O Indra, the Soma drops have been poured forth for you with prostrations,
by those who perform the great sacrificial offering.
Being purified in the eternal form, he flows toward all splendors;
like a hero among cattle, he stands firm.
Like the swelling ridge of heaven, the stream of the pressed juice overflows for the wise ordainer.
He flows effortlessly through the filter. O Soma, being purified for the sake of the wise among living men,
you run through the sheep’s wool.
Like rivers flowing down a slope, the impetuous Soma drops, slaying the Vṛtras, have been let loose like swift steeds. The pressed drops flow forth like rains upon the earth.
The Somas have flowed toward Indra.
With its surging wave, the exhilarating, intoxicating Soma flows through the filter,
driving away the demons, seeking the gods.
He rushes into the jars; he is poured out across the filter;
he grows strong through hymns at the sacrifices. O Soma, ascending above the three luminous realms, you shine up toward heaven.
Impelling the sun, you have sent it forth like a driver.
The inspired poets, the singers, have shouted their praise at the head of the sacrifice,
bestowing what is dear upon your eye.
Thee, the prize-winning one, the heroes—the inspired sages seeking aid—purify with their prayers for the service of the gods.
Flow along the stream of honey; as the sharp one, thou hast taken thy seat in the common dwelling-place.
Beautiful for the sake of the Truth, for drinking;
being pressed, Soma, dwelling on the mountains, has flowed through the filter. In your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
You are the sage, you are the seer; the sweetness is born from the soma-juice.
In the exhilarations... All the gods, acting in unison, have partaken of your draught.
In his exhilarations... [He] who holds in his two hands all desirable treasures;
in his exhilarations...
He who milks these two great worlds, heaven and earth, like two mother cows, in his exhilarations...
He who instantly flows around both worlds with his strengths.
RV_09.018.06.2 {08} In the exhilarations...
RV_09.018.07.1 {08} He, the vigorous one, bellowing as he is purified within the jars, RV_09.018.07.2 {08} In the exhilarations...
O Soma, whatever wondrous, praiseworthy wealth there is in heaven and on earth—
that, being purified, bring to us. For you two, O Indra and Soma, are the lords of light and the lords of cattle.
O Lords, cause our prayers to swell with nourishment.
Purifying himself among living beings like a thundering bull upon the sacred grass,
the golden-hued one has settled in his place.
The prayers have lowed over the seed of the bull;
the mothers [lowed] over their son, the calf. Will he, being purified, bestow the germ upon those who long for the male?
Those who milk the bright milk—O Pavamāna, bestow wealth upon us; O Lord of the Waters, grant strength to those who stand firm, and instill fear in our enemies.
Find riches for us.
O Soma, strike down the virility of the enemy, strike down his strength, and strike down his vigor—
whether he be far away or near at hand.
The Sage flows forth through the woollen filter for the banquet of the gods.
Overcoming all adversaries,
for he, as Pavamāna, indeed bestows upon his singers thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle.
You touch all things with your mind; you flow clear through our hymns.
O Soma, find for us glorious renown. Flow toward us with great fame and enduring wealth for our patrons.
Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Soma, like a king of goodly vows, you have entered our songs;
being purified, O wondrous bearer, [you flow].
Like a bearer difficult to overcome in the waters, being cleansed by the two hands,
Soma settles in the vessels.
Playful like a liberal sacrificer, O Soma, you go toward the filter.
Bestowing great heroic power upon the singer.
These Soma drops run forth for Indra, the impetuous ones, exhilarating and finding the light of heaven.
Driving away assailants, finding wide space for the one who presses the juice, they themselves bestow long life upon the singer.
The drops of Soma play at will, all together toward their single common dwelling-place.
The waves of the river have flowed forth;
these purifying drops have attained all desirable things, like well-harnessed horses to a chariot.
O drops of Soma, bestow upon this man a golden-hued seer to point out the way,
he who is hostile toward us.
Like the Rbhus, bestow a new chariot and a brilliant purpose to point out the way.
O bright ones, flow clear with your flood!
These very ones have lowed; like prize-winning steeds, they have reached the goal and poured forth their inspired thought from the existent.
These Soma juices, swift as chariots, have rushed forward like prize-winning steeds; once let loose, they have sped away.
These are like the wide-reaching winds, like the rains of Parjanya.
Like the flickering flames of fire,
these purified Soma juices, mixed with curds, have spread through the inspired thoughts of the wise seers by means of their poetic insight.
These immortal ones, purified, have not grown weary though they have sped forth; desiring to sacrifice, they traverse the paths through the mid-air.
Striving toward the heights, these [Somas] have pervaded the backs of heaven and earth.
And even this highest realm;
they have followed along the downward slopes the highest thread being stretched out;
and even this most worthy of praise.
O Soma, you held for the Paṇis the wealth consisting of cattle;
you made that stretched thread resound. The swift Somas have been poured forth in a stream of the exhilarating honeyed juice.
Toward all poetic inspirations,
the ancient Āyus have taken their newest step;
they have brought forth the Sun for the sake of splendor.
O Pavamāna, bring to us the wealth of the non-sacrificing enemy;
provide us with food accompanied by progeny. The vital Soma drops flow for the exhilarating intoxication.
Toward the honey-dripping vat,
Soma flows, the sustainer, bestowing vital power and essence;
he is the possessor of great heroism, the protector against curses.
O Soma, you flow for Indra, for the gods, as one who shares the feast; O Indu, you desire to win the prize of strength.
Having drunk of its exhilarating draughts, Indra has overcome his enemies without opposition.
He has struck and he shall strike now.
The Soma drops, the purifying juices, have flowed forth;
being mixed with milk, they are cleansed in the waters.
The cows have flowed toward him like waters going down a slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.
O Pavamāna Soma, you flow forth for Indra to drink.
Guided by men, you are led forth. O Soma, exhilarating to men, flow for the sake of the subduer of peoples— you who are a winner of booty and worthy of universal acclaim.
O Indu, when pressed by the stones, you flow through the filter; you are ready for the abode of Indra.
Flow on, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, you who are to be celebrated with hymns.
Pure, purifying, and wonderful;
pure and purifying is Soma called, the pressed sweetness, the friend of the gods and the slayer of the wicked.
Flow on, O tawny one, accomplishing skill for the gods to drink;
flow as a gladdening draught for the Maruts and for Vāyu.
O Pavamāna, impelled by prayer, bellowing toward your place of origin.
By the cosmic law, enter Vāyu;
the bull, the sage, the beloved, shines together with the gods in his dwelling-place—
the slayer of Vṛtra, most eager for the feast of the gods.
Entering all forms, being purified, the beloved one goes to where the immortals sit. The ruddy Soma, generating songs, flows for the sake of long life.
Going toward Indra, possessing the wisdom of a seer;
flow, O most exhilarating sage, through the filter with your stream,
to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
The inspired poets have milked the vigorous steed from the lap of Aditi with their subtle meditation.
The cows have lowed toward him, the inexhaustible one who flows in a thousand streams.
The drop, the sustainer from heaven;
him, the ordainer, they have urged with wisdom, the purifying one, across the sky— the supporter, the provider of much nourishment.
Him, dwelling with the thought of Vivasvat, they have magnified with their two arms;
him, the infallible lord of speech. Him, the tawny one, his sisters urge on with stones upon the ridge.
Desirable, far-seeing—
O Pavamāna, the wise ones urge you on, you who increase with song,
O Indu, the exhilarating one for Indra.
This seer, highly praised, flows over the filter; purifying himself, he strikes away the enemies.
This winner of light is poured out for Indra and Vāyu.
In the filter, he is the accomplisher of skill;
this bull, the head of heaven, is led forth by the men, pressed out— the Soma, the knower of all, within the wooden vessels.
Seeking cattle and seeking gold, this Pavamāna has bellowed; Indu is the ever-conquering, the unsubdued. This Pavamāna shines with the sun upon the sky.
In the filter, the exhilarating, intoxicating juice.
This vigorous, tawny bull has flowed into the mid-air; being purified, the drop goes toward Indra.
This vigorous steed, sent forth by the men, the all-knowing lord of the mind, rushes through the sheep’s wool filter. This Soma, pressed for the gods, has flowed into the filter.
Entering all abodes,
this immortal god,
the slayer of Vṛtra and the greatest invoker of the gods, shines forth upon his station.
This bull, bellowing loudly, guided by the ten sisters,
rushes toward the wooden vats.
This Pavamāna, the all-seeing one, has caused the sun to shine.
Knowing all, he pervades all abodes.
This powerful, invincible Soma flows while being purified— the friend of the gods, the slayer of the wicked.
The streams of the pressed bull have flowed forth with vigor,
as he stands ready to serve the gods. The wise priests, chanting with their song, groom the steed.
Light has been born, worthy of praise.
O Soma, Lord of abundant wealth, these things are easy for you to overcome as you purify yourself; swell the ocean, which is worthy of praise.
Winning all treasures, flow onward with your stream, O Soma;
drive away our enemies together. Protect us well from the stingy man, from the shout of anyone whatsoever.
So that we may be released from reproach.
O Indu, flow with your stream, purifying the earthly and celestial wealth;
bring us resplendent vigor.
The streams of this impetuous one have flowed freely through the filter;
being purified, he sends forth his voice. Indu, urged by the pressers and being cleansed, goes bellowing along.
He sends forth his voice,
his vital power. O Soma, flow for us with your stream— [a stream] that brings strength for the conquest of men, rich in heroes, and much-desired.
Soma, being purified, has flowed forth with his stream;
he has settled within the wooden vats. They urge you, the most honey-sweet, the tawny one, into the waters with the pressing-stones.
O Indu, flow for Indra to drink.
Press out the most honey-sweet Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt— the lovely, exhilarating draught for the host [of Maruts].
The Soma drops, well-intentioned and purifying, have flowed forth; they create wealth that brings conscious awareness.
O Indu, from heaven and from earth, become the increaser of our splendor.
You are the lord of spoils.
To you the winds are dear; for you the rivers flow;
O Soma, they increase your greatness.
Swell up; let virile strength gather from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of the prize.
For you, O tawny one, the cows have milked out imperishable ghee and milk.
Upon the highest summit,
O Indu, Lord of the world who art well-armed, we desire thy friendship.
The Soma drops, distilling rapture, have flowed forth for our patrons’ glory at the sacrifice.
Then the maidens of Trita urge the tawny one with the pressing-stones.
The drop for Indra to drink;
like a swan to its flock, it has caused the prayer of every man to resound;
it is anointed with milk like a steed.
Beholding both worlds, O Soma, you flow like a deer that has been startled;
settling in the womb of Truth. The cows have lowed toward him, as a woman toward her beloved lover.
He has come to the race, as if to a prize already set before him.
Bestow upon us glorious fame— both for our patrons and for me— and grant us gain, wisdom, and renown.
The Soma juices, the inspired poets, flow forth like the waves of the waters,
like buffaloes toward the forests.
The tawny, bright drops flow toward the wooden vats in a stream of the Eternal Law (*ṛta*).
They have flowed forth toward booty consisting of cattle.
The pressed Soma juices flow for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, the Maruts, and Viṣṇu.
Three voices rise up; the milch-cows low. The tawny one goes, bellowing loudly. The youthful mothers of Truth, the sacred prayers, have sung in praise.
They groom the Child of Heaven.
O Soma, flow for us from every side with wealth from the four oceans, bringing thousands.
Being pressed, Indu flows forth in a stream, urged onward; he breaks down even the firm things by his might.
Pressed for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, and the Maruts.
Soma flows for Viṣṇu.
With stones they press the bull-like Soma, which is joined with the bulls; they milk out the milk with skillful power.
He becomes the one to be purified for Trita; he becomes the exhilarating draught for Indra.
The tawny steed is anointed with beautiful forms.
For him, the sons of Pṛśni milk out the summit of Truth.
The oblation is beautiful and most dear.
These unerring songs flow together toward him;
he has lowed like milch-cows and mares.
Flow toward us with your stream, O Pavamāna, bestowing vast wealth, by which you may find light for us.
O Indu, stir the ocean; flow on, you who cause all things to tremble.
The sustainer of wealth for us by his might; with you as our hero, may we, full of heroes, overcome those who attack us; let there flow for us desirable things.
The Soma-drop, desiring to win, sends forth its vigor as a seer who wins the prize; knowing the sacred laws and his weapons,
we clothe him with our songs as he purifies his voice, moving it to and fro.
Soma, the lord of the people;
he under whose law all men abide, the lord of the sacred order, as he is being purified, O possessor of abundant wealth.
Like a chariot-horse, the pressed juice has been released into the filter for the two bowls; like a prize-winning steed, he has stepped onto the goal-line.
O Soma, you who are the bearer and the watchful one, flow on for the sake of the gods.
Toward the vat that drips with honey—
O ancient Pavamāna, shine forth lights for us;
impel us toward wisdom and skill.
Being beautified by those who love the cosmic order (*ṛta*), being cleansed by the two hands,
he flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
That Soma, bestowing all treasures belonging to heaven and earth upon the donor, flows on.
Let those belonging to the intermediate space flow forth;
O Soma, Lord of Might, you ascend to the back of heaven, seeking horses, seeking cattle, and seeking heroes.
Pressed for the sake of drinking, that bull, Soma, flows through the filter; warding off the demons, he seeks the gods.
Far-sighted and golden-hued, he flows through the filter, the sustainer.
Crying out toward his place of origin,
that prize-winning steed, Pavamāna, rushes through the luminous realms of heaven; the slayer of demons, he flows through the woolly filter.
Pavamāna, upon the high ridge of Trita, caused the sun to shine together with his kinsmen.
He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the bull, the pressed one, the finder of wide space, and the invincible.
Soma has sped forth like a prize-winning steed;
that god, impelled by the sage, rushes toward the wooden vats,
the drop for Indra with great power.
This very bull, this chariot, flows through the sheep’s woolly filter,
going toward thousandfold booty.
The maidens of Trita urge this tawny one forward with the pressing-stones.
The drop for Indra to drink.
Him, the ten active fingers thoroughly cleanse;
with them he adorns himself for exhilaration.
Like a falcon, he settles among the human clans; like a lover going to his mistress, he approaches them. This exhilarating juice, the child of heaven, looks down from on high.
The drop that has entered the filter—
this tawny one, the sustainer, flows for the drinking, having been pressed; bellowing toward his beloved place of origin.
Flow swiftly, O thou of lofty thought, with thy beloved form,
to where they say the gods are. Preparing what was unprepared, bestowing nourishment upon the people.
Flow down the rain from heaven.
The pressed juice goes into the filter, assuming brilliance by its might,
looking out and shining brightly.
This is he who, with rapid course, from heaven through the filter has flowed forth upon the wave of the river.
Invoking him from afar and from near at hand, he has been pressed.
For Indra, the honey is poured out. United, they have sung; they urge the tawny one with the stones.
Sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
Being purified, the far-seeing one has stepped upon all adversaries;
they adorn the sage with their prayers.
The ruddy one has mounted his seat; the pressed juice, as a bull, shall go to Indra.
He sits in his firm seat.
Now, O Indu, O Soma, flow for us from every side with great wealth, a thousandfold.
O Soma Pavamāna, O Indu, bring all splendors;
find for us nourishments in thousands. As you are being purified, bring wealth and heroic strength to our singer.
Exalt the songs of the singer. O Indu, being purified, bring us, O Soma, doubly-mighty wealth,
O bull, O Indu, wealth worthy of hymns.
Those who have advanced like impetuous bulls,
brilliant and tireless, driving away the black skin; we meditate upon a path of well-being that crosses over the bridge of the malevolent.
Overpowering the lawless Dasyu,
the roar of the mighty Pavamāna is heard like the sound of rain; lightnings move across the sky.
Flow forth, O Indu, bringing great nourishment, accompanied by cattle, gold, horses, and strength, once you have been pressed.
Flow on, O most observant one, and fill the two great worlds, heaven and earth.
Like the Dawn and the Sun with their rays,
O Soma, flow around us on every side with a stream that grants us protection,
as rivers fill the earth with moisture.
Generating the lights of heaven, generating the sun in the waters,
the tawny one, clothing himself in the cows, has driven them forth. This god, according to the ancient hymn, [has come] from among the gods.
The pressed juice flows in a stream. For him who has grown strong and is victorious, the Soma drops, possessing thousandfold power, flow forth for the winning of the prize.
Yielding his ancient milk, he is poured out across the filter;
bellowing, he has brought the gods into being.
Toward all desirable things, toward the gods who increase the cosmic order, he flows.
Soma, being purified, flows onward.
O Soma, being pressed, flow for us with cattle, with heroes, with horses, and with booty; purify yourself, bringing great nourishments.
He who, like a steed, is cleansed by the milk-cows for exhilaration, he who is desirable—
him we clothe with our songs of praise. All our songs, seeking his aid, adorn him in the ancient manner.
The drop for Indra to drink.
Being purified, the beloved Soma goes forth, adorned with songs,
[the work] of the sage Medhyātithi.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth accompanied by great splendor; O Indu, [wealth] possessing a thousandfold luster.
Like a courser seeking booty, the Indu neighs loudly within the filter.
When he, seeking the gods, flows forth; flow for the winning of booty, for the increase of the singer who praises you;
O Soma, bestow upon us great heroic strength.
O Indu, for our great expansion, you flow forth like a wave,
bearing it toward the gods with unwearied speed.
Pleased by our hymn and established by our prayer, Soma is sent forth in the distance.
The sage, with the stream of the inspired singer,
this watchful one among the gods, goes pressed into the filter; Soma, the far-seeing, moves onward.
Flow for us, seeking booty, making our sacrifice beautiful;
he who possesses the sacred grass invites [the gods].
As a hero among sages, ever-increasing, flow for us for the sake of Bhaga and Vāyu.
Soma has led us among the gods. May he, the finder of wisdom, the best knower of the path, win for us today strength and lofty fame for the sake of gaining wealth.
Flow on for exhilaration, you who behold men, for the feast of the gods;
O Indu, flow for Indra’s drinking. Flow for us toward the mission of a messenger; you bestow gifts upon Indra.
[Bring] the gods for our friends as the best [of all].
And we anoint you, the ruddy one, with milk for exhilaration;
open wide for us the doors to wealth.
The vigorous steed has passed through the filter, as one goes to the pole on a journey;
Indu rules among the gods. Together the friends have shouted for him as he sports in the wood, passing through the sheep’s fleece.
They have sung to Indu with a boat. Flow forth with that stream by which, when drunk, O Indu,
you grant great heroic power to the singer.
The drops have been poured forth for the feast of the gods, like successful steeds,
flowing, increasing upon the mountains.
Adorned, the drops are like a maiden who honors her father’s house.
The Soma drops have been poured forth for Vāyu. These Soma drops, the Indu-drops, rich in nourishment and pressed into the vessels,
strengthen Indra with their ritual acts.
O dexterous ones, run hither; seize the bright juices with the *manthin* vessel.
Mix the exhilarating draught with milk.
Flow on, O winner of wealth, bestowing great bounty.
O Soma, find the path for us!
These ten fingers cleanse him who is worthy of cleansing, the purifying Pavamāna,
the intoxicating draught for Indra.
By this well-performed deed, Soma has grown even greater;
exhilarated, he acts like a bull.
His deeds and those yet to be done are manifest as the destruction of the Dasyus.
Boldly he gathers the debts;
then Soma becomes the Indrian juice, the thunderbolt that wins a thousandfold,
when his hymn of praise is born.
The seer himself, as the ordainer, seeks treasure for the sage when he polishes his prayers.
Desiring to win riches, he is like one seeking swift horses in the contests for booty.
We belong to those who have been victorious in battles.
We, through our skillful deeds, worship you— the beloved one who bears manly powers in the assemblies of the great heaven.
The exhilarating drink, which has gathered boldness, is worthy of praise, possesses most mighty ordinances, and desires to shatter a hundred fortresses—
from that, O wise one, [I invoke] you, the king of wealth, from heaven.
The unwavering, fair-winged one has brought [him] for every beholder of heaven— the common protector of the cosmic order who traverses the mid-air;
the hero has brought him.
Then, being urged forth, he attained his Indra-power and his greater majesty—
the one who brings aid to men and moves among all people.
Flow for us, bringing rain, with a wave of waters from the sky.
Free from disease, bringing abundant nourishment— flow with that stream by which the cattle may come here,
the kinsmen, to our home.
Flow with a stream of clarified butter, you who are most beloved by the gods at the sacrifices;
flow for us, bringing rain.
Flow through the filter for our nourishment, purifying yourself with your stream.
May the gods indeed hear us!
Pavamāna has flowed forth, striking down the demons,
illuminating lights as he did of old.
Your vital powers surge upward like the roar of a river’s wave;
sharpen the point of your arrow. At your impulse, three voices eager for the sacrifice rise up.
When they urge the beloved tawny one through the sheep’s wool filter with the stones upon the ridged back of the sheep,
O Pavamāna, you who drip sweetness.
Flow, O most exhilarating sage, through the filter in a stream,
to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
Flow, O most exhilarating one, being anointed with milk and with ointments.
O Indu, [flow] for Indra to drink. O Adhvaryu, pour the Soma pressed with stones into the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink.
Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the supreme nectar of heaven— the Soma most rich in sweetness. O Indu, those gods partake of that sweet juice of yours.
The Maruts [are] of Pavamāna.
O Soma, for you, being pressed, increase the zealous one for exhilaration;
O Bull, [you do so] for the sake of aiding the praiser.
Flow toward us, O far-seeing one, with your stream, being pressed through the filter— toward booty and toward glory. The dweller in heaven, winner of wealth, has brought us strength with his juice.
Being pressed, flow into the filter;
through your ancient paths, flow beloved through the sheep’s wool,
with a thousand streams in a continuous line.
Like a charioteer, make our sacrifice swing; O Indu, make the gift swing.
With your weapons, O wielder of weapons, make it swing.
O Much-invoked One, strike down the strength of these people for the sake of Indu.
Whoever seeks to harm us—
O Indu, flow for us with a hundred aids, or even a thousand of your pure streams, bestowing abundant wealth.
Your vital powers have risen up, O wielder of the stone, shattering the *rakṣas* demons;
drive away those who are our rivals. With this very might you have struck them down when the chariots met and the prize was staked.
I praise you with a fearless heart; no one of evil intent can violate the ordinances of this Pavamāna. Break him who attacks you!
They urge him on— the tawny, exhilarating steed— into the rivers, the Indu that brings intoxication for Indra. Following his ancient splendor, the bold ones have milked out the bright [Soma].
The milk belongs to the seer who wins a thousandfold.
This one, visible like the sun, runs toward the lakes and the seven downward paths to heaven.
Purifying himself, this Soma stands above all worlds as our god, like the Sun. Flow around us for the feast of the gods, bringing strengths consisting of cattle.
O Indu, being purified, desiring Indra— flow around us with your juice, yielding grain after grain and nourishment after nourishment,
O Soma, and all auspicious blessings.
O Indu, as is your praise, as is the birth of your juice,
so sit upon the beloved sacrificial grass. And flow for us, O Soma, finding cattle and finding horses, with your exhilarating juice.
Most swiftly through these days— [O Soma],
you who conquer but are not conquered, who strikes down the enemy by attacking him— flow on as the winner of thousands!
Soma, the swift one, flows through the filter according to the great *ṛta*,
driving away the demons and seeking the gods.
When Soma flows toward the prize, his hundred active streams flow forth.
Entering into friendship with Indra,
the ten maidens have sung out to you like a lover; O Soma, you are being purified for the sake of winning the prize.
O Indu, flow around as something sweet for Indra and Viṣṇu;
protect the men, the singers, from distress.
Your unceasing streams go forth like rains from heaven.
Toward thousandfold booty;
beholding all dear poetic insights, he flows on,
the tawny one, brandishing his weapons.
Being cleansed by the Āyus, like a king of noble vows, he,
like a hawk, settles among the woods.
May he [bring] all treasures for us from heaven and from the earth.
O Indu, being purified, bring [us wealth].
Crossing over, that exhilarating one flows; the stream of the pressed juice flows— crossing over, that exhilarating one flows.
The Dawn knows of treasures; O Goddess, she knows the protection for the mortal man.
Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows onward.
From the two tawny ones who favor men, we receive many thousands.
Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows; he for whom we receive thirty times a thousand in succession—
crossing over, the exhilarating one flows.
Flow on, O Soma, winner of cattle, winner of horses, winner of all, winner of joy;
bring us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Flow on, O invincible one, for the waters; flow on for the plants.
Flow clear for the sake of the two bowls.
O Soma, as you flow, cross over all difficulties;
as a seer, sit down upon the sacred grass.
O Pavamāna, finding the light of heaven, as soon as you were born, you became great;
O Indu, you surpass all things. Sing forth with the *gāyatra* hymn to Pavamāna, who beholds all people.
The drop with a thousand eyes—
Thee, who hast a thousand eyes and a thousandfold wealth, They have purified through the woolen filter.
Pavamāna has flowed through the fleece; he rushes toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra.
O Soma, most active one, flow auspiciously for the sake of Indra’s bounty.
Bring us seed accompanied by progeny!
Flow around with this invitation, O Indu, you who, in your exhilarations, struck down ninety-nine [foes].
Immediately before this, for Divodāsa who thus meditated, you struck down Śambara; and then Turvaśa and Yadu as well.
O Indu, finder of horses, bestow upon us wealth in horses, cattle, and gold.
Flow forth thousandfold nourishing foods.
We choose for ourselves the friendship of you, Pavamāna, as you rise up toward the filter.
O Soma, those waves of yours which flow across the filter in a stream—
with them, O Soma, show us mercy.
As you purify yourself, bring us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons.
O Soma, you are the sovereign lord over all. The ten fingers cleanse him, whose mother is the river; he has appeared together with the Ādityas.
Together with Indra and Vāyu, the pressed juice goes into the filter;
together with the rays of Sūrya, it flows. Flow for us as honey-sweet for Bhaga, Vāyu, and Pūṣan.
He is dear to Mitra and Varuṇa. High above is the birth of your juice; seated in heaven, it has been bestowed upon the earth—terrible protection and great renown.
Through him, we, desiring to win, acquire all these splendors of men, O noble one. May he [grant them] to us for Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts.
Flow around us, finding wide space.
The gods have come to the Soma-drop— born as the one who crosses the waters, adorned with milk, the breaker of obstacles.
May our songs strengthen him, as mother cows their calf—he who wins the heart of Indra.
Flow for us, O Soma; milk out for us nourishing food that swells with abundance.
Increase the ocean worthy of praise.
Pavamāna has generated from heaven a wondrous sound like thunder,
the great light of Vaiśvānara.
O King, your exhilarating juice, as you are being purified, is free from evil;
it flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
O Pavamāna, your juice, which is skillful and radiant, shines forth.
The universal light for the sight of heaven. Flow on with that exhilarating juice of yours which is most excellent, O invoker of the gods, slayer of the wicked.
Slayer of Vṛtra, the unfriendly foe; winner of booty day by day;
thou art the winner of cattle and the winner of horses. Be mingled with our offerings, O ruddy one, like cows that are easy to tend.
Sitting like a hawk upon his nest,
flow on, you who aided Indra to slay Vṛtra when he had enclosed the great waters.
O bounteous Soma, may we, possessing brave sons, win riches.
Being purified, you increase our songs. Protected by you and through your favor, may we be victorious over those who attack us.
O Soma, be watchful in our sacred rites! Striking down the adversaries, Soma flows clear, driving away the stingy ones as he goes to the appointed place of Indra.
O Pavamāna, bring us great wealth; slay our enemies.
O Indu, grant us glory accompanied by heroic sons.
Not even a hundred deceivers can obstruct you when you desire to bestow bounty.
When, being purified, you exert yourself like a champion; flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull. Make us glorious among the people;
strike down all those who hate us.
In this friendship of yours, O Indu, in your supreme splendor, may we overcome those who attack us.
Those terrible weapons of yours which are sharp for striking— [in them may we find protection].
Protect us from every reproach.
These swift drops have been poured through the filter,
toward all auspicious fortunes.
Warding off many misfortunes, providing easy paths for our offspring, O possessors of strength, you create continuous prosperity for our horses;
bestowing wide space for our cattle, they flow toward our hymn of praise.
May we receive from you a continuous stream of nourishment.
This Soma-stalk, the skillful one dwelling on the mountains, has been pressed for intoxication; like a hawk, it has settled in its place.
The bright juice, beloved by the gods, shaken in the waters and pressed by men—
the cows sweeten it with their milk. Then, like drivers [beautifying] a horse, they have adorned it for the sake of immortality.
The essence of honey at the shared feast;
those streams of yours, O Indu, dripping with sweetness, which were poured forth for our aid— with them you have settled in the filter.
Flow for Indra to drink, passing through the sheep’s wool filter; settling in your place within the wooden vessels.
O Indu, flow around as the sweetest draught for the Aṅgirases.
Finding wide space, [he provides] ghee and milk.
This Pavamāna, set in motion and active among the people, takes notice; being urged forward, he manifests his great kinship.
This bull, whose law is manly, Pavamāna, the slayer of the ill-spoken, shall bring riches to the donor.
Flow hitherward, bringing thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle and horses.
Rich in splendor, desired by many—
this very one is poured out all around, being cleansed by the living priests; he is the wide-striding one, possessing the wisdom of a seer.
With a thousand aids and a hundredfold wealth, the measurer of the realm, the sage,
the exhilarating juice flows for Indra.
Born through song, praised here, the drop is set apart for Indra.
Like one entering a dwelling with a noble womb,
the pressed Soma, being purified by the men, has sped forth like toward booty,
to sit within the vessels with skillful power.
Him they yoke to the three-backed, triple-seated chariot to go forth, by means of the seven inspirations of the seers.
O pressers, [yoke] him, the winner of wealth, the swift one, for the sake of the prize-winning race.
Drive forth the tawny, vigorous steed.
Having been pressed, entering the jar, he flows toward all splendors;
like a hero among the cattle, he stands firm.
O Indu, for your exhilaration, the Āyus milk out the milk for you;
the gods [milk] the honey for the gods. Release for us into the filter the Soma that is most rich in sweetness.
To the gods, the one most heard by the gods—
these Soma juices have been poured forth while being praised for great renown, with the stream of the most intoxicating [Soma].
Flowing pure, you rush toward the cattle-rich spoils for our enjoyment;
winning the prize, flow all around us. And flow for us with all food-offerings rich in cattle, accompanied by hymns of praise.
Praised by Jamadagni,
flow on as the leader of our speech, O Soma, with your wondrous aids,
toward all poetic inspirations.
You, the foremost, stirring the waters of the ocean with your voice,
flow on, O you who set all things in motion!
O Sage Soma, these worlds stand ready for your greatness.
The rivers flow for you; like rains from heaven, your unceasing streams go forth toward the bright surface-covering.
For Indra, purify the Soma-drop, the fierce one, the means of success for skill;
[purify] the lord who bestows wealth.
O Pavamāna, the sage of Truth, Soma has settled upon the filter.
Bestowing excellent heroic power upon the singer.
Flow on, O Soma, bringing thousandfold wealth and excellent heroic power; bestow upon us glorious renown.
You swell with nourishment and vigor for Indra, you who are most intoxicating;
you settle within the vessels. Pressed for Indra and Viṣṇu, Soma has flowed into the jar.
Honey-sweet for Vāyu;
these swift, brown Soma drops have been poured forth in a stream of *ṛta*, passing over all obstacles.
Increasing Indra, crossing the waters, making all things Aryan, they strike down the stingy ones.
Pressed, the brown drops flow toward their own space through the mid-air.
The drops go toward Indra. Flow with this stream by which you caused the sun to shine, being urged on through the human waters.
Pavamāna has yoked Etaśa, the steed of Sūrya, at his will,
so that he may travel through the mid-air.
And he has yoked those ten bay mares of Sūrya for the journey.
The drop, crying out "Indra!"—
pour it out for Vāyu, the exhilarating juice, for Indra;
pour it through the sheep's wool filter.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth that is difficult to surpass— wealth that is hard for the enemy to seize.
Flow toward us with thousandfold riches, consisting of cattle and horses.
Toward booty and toward glory.
Soma, like the divine Sun, flows when pressed by the stones,
bestowing his juice within the jar.
These bright ones, by the stream of *ṛta*, have flowed toward the stations of the Āryas,
bringing strength rich in cattle.
Pressed for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, are these Soma juices mixed with curds.
They have flowed across the filter.
O Soma, most rich in sweetness, flow for the sake of wealth into the filter— flow as the exhilarating draught that is most beloved by the gods.
The Āyus cleanse him, the tawny, vigorous steed in the rivers— the Indu, who brings no stinginess to Indra. Flow on, O Soma, bringing gold, horses, and heroic sons.
Bring us strength consisting of cattle!
Pour out for Indra the most honey-sweet [draught], like one seeking prize-winning strength upon the sheep’s wool [sieve].
The inspired poets, seeking aid, purify with their prayers the Sage who is worthy of being cleansed;
the Bull, bellowing loudly, flows forth.
With their prayers, they purify the bull-like Soma, the swift-crosser of waters, by means of the stream of *ṛta*.
The sages have chanted their hymns together with devotion.
Flow on, O Soma, for the sake of the gods; let your exhilaration reach Indra. Ascend to Vāyu according to the sacred law.
O Pavamāna Soma, you bestow wealth worthy of renown;
as the beloved one, enter the ocean.
Striking down adversaries, O Soma, you flow as the exhilarating finder of wisdom.
Drive away the people who do not seek the gods.
The purifying Soma drops, bright and radiant, have been let loose toward all poetic inspirations.
The purifying, swift, and brilliant drops have been let loose, O Indu,
striking away all enemies.
The purifying ones have flowed forth from heaven and from the mid-air.
Upon the ridge of the earth,
O Soma, being purified in your stream, O Indu, strike away all enemies;
slay the demons, O you of noble power.
Striking down the Rākṣasas, O Soma, flow hither with loud roaring, bringing forth brilliant and most excellent vigor.
Bestow upon us, O Soma, the treasures of heaven and of earth.
O Indu, [flow] toward all desirable things.
O Soma, you are a bull, resplendent; O God, you are a bull whose laws are bull-like.
As a bull, you uphold the sacred ordinances.
Thy virile power is manly strength; thou art a bull, a bull in the wood, a bull in thy exhilaration.
O Bull, truly thou art a bull.
Like a neighing horse, the bull has bellowed; O Indu, thou hast gathered together the cows and the steeds.
Open for us the doors to wealth.
The Soma juices, swift and powerful, have been poured forth— desiring cattle, desiring horses, bright, heroic, and rapid.
Being beautified by those who love the *ṛta*, being cleansed by the two hands, they flow through the fleecy filter.
These Soma juices bestow all treasures belonging to heaven and earth upon the donor.
Let those dwelling in the intermediate space flow forth; O all-knowing one, the streams of thee, the purifying one,
have been released like the rays of the sun.
Making yourself a banner from the sky, you flow toward all forms;
O Soma, you swell like the ocean.
Being urged forward, O Pavamāna, you send forth your voice across the firmament.
The divine Sūrya has stepped forth for us;
the conscious drop has flowed, beloved by the thoughts of the seers,
like a charioteer releasing his horse.
Your wave, which flows through the filter, seeking the gods, has moved all around;
settling into the womb of Truth.
Flow for us through the filter as that exhilarating juice which most invites the gods.
O Indu, flow for Indra to drink. Flow with your stream for nourishment, being purified by the wise;
O Indu, come hither with your luster.
Purifying yourself, O lover of songs, create wide space and strength for the people,
O tawny one, as you are released into the milk-mixture. Purifying yourself for the feast of the gods, go to the appointed place of Indra.
Radiant and yoked with the prize-winning steeds,
the swift drops, being urged forward, have been released by the prayer toward the ocean.
Being cleansed, the active drops have gone at will to the ocean,
to the womb of *ṛta*.
Go around us, seeking our favor, with all riches through your power.
Protect us with hero-bearing shelter.
The swift steed, the bearer, neighs as he yokes his station with the chanters,
when he is set upon the ocean.
When the swift one settles in his golden womb of Truth, he leaves behind those who lack understanding.
The longing ones cry out to him; the wise ones worship him.
Those who lack discernment sink down.
O Indu, flow most sweetly for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,
to sit upon the seat of the Truth (Ṛta).
The inspired poets, the wise ordainers who know the sacred word, prepare you;
the Āyus cleanse you thoroughly.
O Sage, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink your essence.
The Maruts [accompany] Pavamāna.
O Soma, being purified, you send forth inspired speech, O Indu, which brings a thousandfold reward.
And so, O Soma, being purified, bring us speech that brings a thousandfold reward and is eager for the sacrifice, O Indu,
you who are invoked by many among these people.
Enter the dear ocean with brilliant radiance, with a song of praise,
and with beauty— the bright Soma juices, mixed with milk.
Urged on by the pressers when he has stepped forth for booty, O prize-winner, like those sitting as eager worshippers—
O Soma, the sage of heaven, coming together for our well-being, [flow] successfully.
Flow on, O Soma, so that you may be seen like the sun!
The rays, the sisters, the kinswomen, urge the hero forward— the great drop, they who desire the great one as their lord.
O Pavamāna, with light after light, as a god from among the gods,
enter into all treasures.
O Pavamāna, [bestow] fair praise, rain, and service upon the gods.
Flow for the sake of gathered nourishment;
for you are a bull by your radiance— we invoke you, the brilliant one, O Pavamāna, with devout thought.
Flow forth, O well-armed one, rejoicing, bestowing heroic strength;
come here, O drops! When you are sprinkled with waters and cleansed by the two hands, flow forth.
With wood you reach your common dwelling-place.
Sing forth, as Vyaśva did, for Soma Pavamāna,
for the great one who possesses a thousand eyes.
Whose honey-dripping, golden hue they urge forth with the stones—
the drop for Indra’s drinking—
of you, that vigorous one who has won all riches, [we partake].
We choose your friendship. Flow on as a bull in your stream, O exhilarating one, for the sake of the Maruts,
bestowing all things by your might.
Thee, O Pavamāna, the sustainer of the two worlds, who beholdest the light of heaven, the prize-winner, I urge on for the sake of booty.
Thus perceived by the inspired song, flow as a tawny steed with thy stream.
Impel our ally in the contests for booty.
O Indu, flow for us as one visible to all, bringing great nourishment;
O Soma, find the path for us.
The pitchers have resounded with the streams of Soma by its might; enter the vessels for Indra’s drinking—
O you whose intoxicating juice they milk out with the stones, sharp and strong.
Flow on as the slayer of the arrogant; the King, being purified, moves by means of inspired thoughts toward the mind,
in order to travel through the intermediate space.
O Indu, bring us hundredfold increase of cattle and noble horses;
bring us fortune for our protection.
O Soma, bring us conquering power and swiftness, like beauty for our splendor.
Pressed for the feast of the gods,
O Soma, flow most brilliantly, roaring toward the wooden vats;
settle there like a falcon upon its nest.
Winning the waters for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, and the Maruts,
Soma flows for Viṣṇu.
Bestowing nourishment upon our offspring and upon us from every side, O Soma!
Flow on, bringing a thousandfold wealth!
Those *soma* juices that are pressed in the distance, those that are pressed nearby, and those that are pressed at Śaryaṇāvat— [flow for them].
Those who are among the Ārjīkas, those who are among the Kṛtvas, those who are in the midst of the dwellings, or those who are among the five peoples—
may they purify for us rain from heaven and heroic strength.
The gods, the drops, are being pressed.
The beloved, golden-hued one flows, being praised by Jamadagni,
as he is urged forward upon the ox-hide.
The bright drops, swift as birds, urged on like coursers,
have been purified in the waters while being mixed.
Thee, such as thou art, the active ones have urged forward at the libations for the service of the gods.
Flow on with this luster;
today we choose for ourselves your skill, which brings bliss,
your vehicle, and the one who is drunk by many and much desired.
Hither [bring] the delightful one, the most excellent, the inspired sage, the wise one; hither [bring] the protector, the one desired by many;
hither [bring] wealth, with good intention, O you of noble power, unto our bodies.
Protecting that which is desired by many;
flow on, O you who belong to all people, toward all poetic insights, as a friend to be praised by his friends.
Through these two abodes of yours, O Pavamāna, you rule over the universe; O Soma, they stand facing toward you.
O Soma, O Sage, you encompass all your stations from every side by means of the seasons as you purify yourself.
Flow on, engendering nourishment for all desirable things,
as a friend for the sake of his friends' aid.
Your bright rays extend across the back of heaven.
O Soma, you are purified by your powers;
O Soma, these seven rivers flow according to your command;
for you the milch-cows run.
O Soma, flow forth with your stream, pressed for Indra, exhilarating;
bestowing imperishable fame.
The seven sisters, urging you on, have sounded you together with their prayers.
They have generated the sage from Vivasvat.
The zealous ones cleanse you upon the sheep’s wool, over the sounding [vessel], when you, the singer, are being anointed in the wood.
O Sage, O powerful one, the streams of you, Pavamāna, have been released like horses seeking renown.
They have flowed toward the vat that drips with honey, through the filter of sheep’s wool.
The prayers have lowed toward the ocean; the drops have gone to their home like milch-cows,
having entered the womb of Truth.

O Indu, flow forth for our great delight; the rivers flow like waters when you clothe yourself in milk. In this friendship of yours, we, desiring to sacrifice and aided by your protection, [attain our goal].
O Indu, we desire your friendship. Flow on for the winning of cattle, O Soma, for the great one who beholds men;
enter into the belly of Indra.
O Soma, you are great, the eldest; O Indra, you are the most powerful among the mighty.
As a warrior, you have always been victorious.
You who are more powerful even than the powerful, and more heroic even than the heroes.

Greater even than those who bestow much, O Soma, you are the one to be magnified; as the impeller of the sun, you are the one to be chosen for the winning of offspring and for the preservation of our bodies.
We choose you for friendship; we choose you for alliance.
O Agni, you purify our lives; pour forth upon us strength and nourishment, and drive misfortune far away.
Agni is the seer, the purifying one, the domestic priest for the five peoples.
We pray to him, the great hunter. O Agni, you who are skillful in action, purify yourself for us, bestowing splendor and heroic vigor;
grant me wealth and nourishment.
Pavamāna flows across all obstacles toward our fair praise, visible to all like the sun.
Being cleansed by the Āyus, he is provided with nourishment and established for the sake of enjoyment.
The drop, far-seeing, has looked out across [the worlds].
Pavamāna has generated the great *ṛta*, the bright light;
he has struck down the black darknesses.

Of Pavamāna, the tawny one, as he strikes down [the obstacles], the golden drops have been released— swift ones with rapid radiance. Pavamāna is the best of charioteers, most beautifully praised by the beautiful ones.
Hariścandra is the host of Maruts.
Pavamāna, the best winner of booty, has pervaded [the world] with his rays,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer.
Being pressed, the Indu flows forth toward the sheep’s-wool filter; being purified, the Indu goes toward Indra. This Soma sports upon the skin of cows, [pressed] by the stones.
They call upon Indra for exhilaration— [O Indra],
whose radiant milk has been brought down from heaven by you, O Pavamāna; with that, be gracious to us so that we may live.

O Soma, you are the sustainer, the delightful and most powerful one at the sacrifice; flow on, bestowing abundant wealth. Pressed out, exhilarating men, you have flowed as the most intoxicating draught.
For Indra, the patron offers the soma-juice with the plant.
Pressed by the stones, flow toward us with a roar—
thou who art the source of brilliant, most excellent strength.
The drop, urged onward, flows through the woollen filters;
the tawny one has bellowed for the prize.
O Indu, you flow through the woolly fleece, bestowing renown and auspicious blessings.
O Soma, distribute wealth consisting of cattle;
O Indu, bring us hundredfold riches, rich in cattle and horses;
O Soma, bestow upon us thousandfold wealth.
The purifying drops, the swift Indus,
have passed through the filter and reached Indra on their courses.
The preeminent, Soma-rich juice, the Indu, is for Indra as of old.
Life flows for life;
the rays of light impel the Sun, the purifying one who drips with sweetness;
they have intoned together with song unto him.
May Pūṣan, whose horses are goats, be our protector on every journey;
may he grant us a share among the maidens.
This Soma flows like ghee, like honey, for the one with matted hair.
May he partake among our maidens.
This [Soma] of yours, O glowing one, being pressed, flows pure like clarified butter.
May he partake among our maidens.
The progenitor of the speech of sages, flow forth, O Soma, in your stream;
you are the bestower of treasures among the gods.
He rushes into the jars; like a falcon, he plunges into his armor.
Roaring toward the wooden vats,
O Soma, your pressed juice has been released; flowing all around into the jar, it rushes like a darting hawk.
Flow, O Soma, gladdening Indra, most rich in sweetness!
They have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like chariots seeking booty.
These pressed juices, most intoxicating and bright, have been released toward Vāyu.
Struck by the pressing-stone and praised, O Soma, you go toward the filter,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer. Struck and praised, this one plunges through the filter.
The slayer of demons [drives] through the woolly filter. Whatever fear dwells nearby or whatever fear finds me here at a distance— O Pavamāna, drive that away!
May that Pavamāna, the all-seeing one, purify us today with his filter— he who is the Purifier.
O Agni, that filter of yours which is spread out within the flame—
Purify us with that sacred prayer (*brahman*).
O Agni, with that purifying power of yours which is radiant, purify us;
purify us with the inspirations of sacred prayer (*brahmasava*).
O God Savitṛ, with both— by means of the filter and by your impulsion— purify me on every side.
O God Savitṛ, purify me with the three most excellent Soma-abodes.
O Agni, purify us with your skills.
May the divine people purify me; may the Vasus purify me with their wisdom.
O All-Gods, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me.
Swell forth, flow onward, O Soma, with all your rays— you,
the most excellent oblation for the gods.
Draw near to the beloved, the praiseworthy, the youthful one who increases through our offerings.
We have come bearing homage.
The axe of Alāyya has perished; O divine Soma, flow pure for him.
O divine Soma, [flow for] even the mouse itself.
He who studies the *pāvamānī* verses— the essence gathered by the seers—
eats everything purified and made savory by Mātariśvan. He who studies the *pāvamānī* verses— the essence gathered by the seers— [attains that].
For him Sarasvatī milks forth milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
Toward the god, the honeyed drops have flowed forth like milch-cows toward us.
Seated upon the sacred grass, eloquent with their udders, they have assumed the bright, flowing robe of the sun.
Roaring loudly, he has bellowed toward the eastern regions; the tawny one, loosening the heights, makes them sweet for his ascent.
Passing through the filter, flowing toward the wide expanse, the god deposits his own shoots according to his will.
The exhilarating draught, which has measured out the two twin sisters who move together, increases with milk and swells the inexhaustible ones.
The Great One, traversing the two boundless realms, has assumed his imperishable luster.
Moving about, seeking strength, he makes the two mothers swell with water; the wise one, by his own power, nourishes his station.
The stalk is adorned with grain as it is led by the men; it unites with its kinsmen and protects the head.
With a skillful mind, the sage is born; he is the embryo of *ṛta*, deposited beyond the twins.
Being young, they two first brought forth that which was hidden in the cave—the birth not cast upward.
The wise ones discerned the form of the joyous one, when the falcon brought the plant from afar.
They cleanse him, the well-increasing one, in the rivers—the yearning stalk that flows around, worthy of praise.
The ten young women cleanse you, O Soma, when you are pressed by the seers, established through hymns and inspired thoughts.
With the fleece-strainers and with invocations of the gods, you are brought forth by the men so that you may burst open for the winning of the prize.
The wise hymns of praise have resounded toward Soma as he proceeds, the one worthy of fair assembly;
He who, immortal and winner of wealth, sends forth his voice from heaven with a honeyed wave in a stream.
This Soma, being purified, sends forth [his light] through the entire mid-air and settles within the jars.
Purified by waters, cleansed by cows, and pressed by stones, may Indu, while being purified, find wide space and what is dear.
Thus, O Soma, as you are being poured out, flow for us, bestowing most wonderful vitality.
We invoke the benevolent Heaven and Earth; O gods, grant us wealth with heroic sons.
Like an arrow set upon the bow, the hymn is aimed; like a calf let loose to the udder of its mother, it flows forth.
Like a wide-streaming cow, she yields at the beginning as she approaches; Soma is impelled within his sacred ordinances.
The hymn is mingled and the sweet mead is poured out; the joyous tongue stirs within the mouth.
Pavamāna, the continuous flow, like a honeyed drop of one who strikes down the foe, flows through the woolen filter.
Seeking a bride, he flows through the sheep’s wool; the daughter of Aditi loosens her bonds for him who goes toward the *ṛta*.
The golden-hued, worshipful, well-restrained exhilaration has stepped forth; sharpening his manly powers, he shines like a buffalo.

The bull bellows; the milch-cows approach him; the goddesses go toward the appointed place of the god. Soma has passed through the bright sheep’s wool; he has clothed himself in his mantle as if it were newly washed.
With an unwashed, radiant garment, the immortal one, golden-hued, has clothed himself in his shining robe.
By his might, he has made the back of heaven his garment for his adornment; he has spread out a covering of mist within the two bowls.
Like the rays of the sun, the exhilarating, sleep-inducing drops rush forth together as they flow.
The swift streams encompass the stretched-out thread; indeed, no state of being flows pure without Indra.
Like swift waters rushing down a slope toward the lowlands, the exhilarating draughts poured forth by the Bull have found their course.

May there be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds in our dwelling; O Soma, may strength and the settled people abide with us. Flow for us, bringing wealth, gold, horses, cattle, barley, and heroic might.
For you, O Soma, are my fathers; you are the heads of heaven, established as the makers of vitality.
These purifying Somas have gone forth toward Indra like chariots toward booty.
Pressed out, they pass through the sheep’s-wool filter; casting off their covering, the tawny ones flow toward the rain.
O Indu, flow clear for the great Indra as one who is most gracious, blameless, and a destroyer of enemies.
Bring radiant treasures to the singer; O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
For him, the thrice-seven milch-cows have milked out the true *āśīr* (mixture) in the ancient sky.
He made four other beautiful worlds for his adornment when he grew strong through the cosmic ordinances (*ṛta*).
Seeking the lovely nectar of immortality, he, by means of his poetic wisdom (*kāvyena*), separated both heaven and earth.
He clothed himself in most brilliant waters with great majesty, when they knew the dwelling place of the god through his glory.
May his rays be immortal and invincible, following after both generations;
by means of these, they purify both human and divine powers, and then the sages took hold of the King.
Being cleansed by the ten skillful workers, he is present together with the middle mothers.
Guarding the sacred laws, the one who possesses the nectar of immortality, the observer of men, beholds both races with his fair countenance.
Being cleansed for the sake of providing Indra’s power, he exults when placed between both ends of heaven and earth.
As a bull, with his vital strength, he drives away the malevolent ones, pointing out the spoils like an archer aiming at his targets.
Beholding his two parents like a young bull, he comes bellowing with a sound like that of the Maruts.

Knowing the primordial truth, the one of excellent wisdom chose the Sun as the hero for his own glorification. The terrifying bull bellows with great power, sharpening his golden horns as he looks abroad.

Soma settles into his well-fashioned womb; the cowhide becomes his bright garment. Purifying himself, the bright one has driven his stainless body onto the back of the sheep’s fleece. Acceptable to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, he is prepared as threefold honey by the skillful workers.
Flow on, O Soma, for the banquet of the gods; as a bull, enter the heart of Indra, the receptacle of Soma.
Before the onset of distress, carry us across all misfortune; for you, the knower of the field, declare the directions to those who ask.
Like a well-urged steed rushing toward the prize, flow on, O Indu, into the belly of Indra.
Like a skilled pilot across the river with a boat, ferry us over; like a hero fighting in battle, protect us from the reviler.
The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is bestowed; the vigorous one seeks his seat. The watchful one guards against the malicious demon.
He makes the golden-hued [Soma] his upper garment, the milk his undergarment, and the sacred prayer (*brahman*) the bright robe for the two vessels.
Like one who ploughs, his strength goes forth bellowing; he casts off this asuric hue of his.
He leaves the covering, he goes to his father’s appointed place; he makes for himself a flowing robe as his own garment.
Pressed by the stones, he flows from the two hands; like a bull, he is stirred by the cloud and moved by the hymn.
He rejoices, he approaches, he succeeds through his song; he cleanses himself in the waters and sacrifices in the full extent of the rite.
They pour out the honeyed draught for the dweller in heaven, the strengthener of the mountains, the conqueror of the palace.
In him, the cows who eat the well-offered oblation mix the head with their vast expanses upon the udder, as the foremost one.
The ten sisters have sent him forth like a chariot from the two poles onto the lap of Aditi.

He has gone; he hastens toward the secret place of the cow, which his inspired thoughts have generated. Like a hawk, the god seeks to settle upon the golden seat, the dwelling-place prepared by wisdom.
They let the beloved one loose upon the sacrificial grass with song; like a horse fit for sacrifice, he goes toward the gods.
The bright red seer of heaven has shone forth from afar; the bull with three backs has bellowed toward the cows.
Leading a thousandfold, moving hither and thither, he shines through many dawns like a singer.
He assumes a brilliant form; his color is this. Wherever he has settled, he drives away the adversaries.
Winning the waters, he goes by his own power to the divine folk; he unites with our fair praise, with that which begins with cattle.
Like a bull moving toward the herds, he has bellowed; he has taken upon himself the splendors of the sun.
The divine eagle looks down upon the earth; Soma beholds all creatures with his wisdom.
They cleanse the golden-hued one; like a ruddy steed, he is yoked; Soma is mingled with the milch-cows in the jar.
He raises up his voice; they urge him on with hymns—the many-lauded one whose dear friends are many indeed.
Many sages speak together when they have poured the Soma into the belly of Indra. When the men with skillful hands cleanse the desirable honey with the ten sisters who share a common nest.
Without resting, he goes beyond the cows, across the roar of the beloved daughter of the Sun.
Vinaṅgrasa brought him what he desired; he dwells together with his twin sisters, his consanguineous kin.

Shaken by men, pressed by the stones upon the sacred grass, the beloved lord of cattle, the ancient, seasonal drop—Soma, rich in wisdom, the accomplisher of man’s sacrifice, pure through prayer, flows for you, O Indra.

Urged by the arms of men, pressed out in a stream, Soma flows for you, O Indra, according to his nature. He has fulfilled our intentions and gathered thoughts at the sacrifice; like a bird alighting on a tree, the tawny one has settled in the two bowls. The skillful, wise poets milk the stalk—the thundering, inexhaustible sage.
Together the cows and the hymns go forth in unison, being born again in the womb of Truth, in the seat of its foundation.
At the navel of the earth, the supporter of the great heaven, he dwells within the waves of the waters and the rivers.
Indra’s thunderbolt, the bull, the possessor of abundant wealth—Soma, the exhilarating one, flows for the heart as something dear.
Flow on, O Soma, through the earthly realm, bestowing gifts upon the singer and the one who shakes [the ladle], O you of noble power.
Do not exclude us from the wealth that reaches our dwelling; may we clothe ourselves in abundant, golden-hued riches.
Come to us, O Indu, bringing a hundredfold gift of horses, a thousandfold gift of cattle, and gold.
Bestow upon me great and wealthy nourishments; O Pavamāna, come to our hymn of praise.
At the snout of the blowing drop, they have sounded together; in the womb of Ṛta, the naves have met.
The Asura has made three heads for himself to grasp; the ships of Truth have carried the doer of good deeds across.
Moving straight forward together like mighty bulls, they have stirred themselves; on the wave of the river, the seekers have caused them to vibrate.
Generating the hymn with streams of honey, they have increased Indra’s beloved body.
Wearing the filter, they sit around the sacred word; their ancient father guards their vow.
