Varuṇa has hidden the great ocean within himself; only the wise have been able to grasp it within its foundations.
At the thousand-streamed source, they have sounded together—the celestial, honey-tongued, and unfailing ones—within the vault of heaven.
His watchful spies do not close their eyes; at every step there are bridgers who bear nooses.
Those who have resounded from above their father and mother, shining with the *ṛc* and consuming the lawless;
by their power, they blow away from the earth and from heaven the black skin hated by Indra.
Those who have resounded from the ancient measure, the controllers of the hymn, the thinkers of the impetuous one.
The blind and the deaf have perished; the evildoers do not cross the path of *Ṛta*.
In the wide-spread filter with a thousand streams, the wise and inspired poets purify their speech.
Their spies are Rudras—vigorous, guileless, swift-moving, fair to behold, and beholders of men.
The guardian of *ṛta*, of noble wisdom, cannot be deceived; he has placed three purifiers within his heart.
Knowing all, he beholds all beings; he strikes down those who lack devotion and those who act without holy vows into the pit.
The thread of *ṛta* is stretched across the purifier at the tip of Varuṇa’s tongue through his creative power (*māyā*).
Even the wise have attained that which they sought; here the powerless one falls from his task.
Like a newborn infant crying out in the wood, the ruddy steed, seeking to win the prize, speeds toward heaven.
He unites with the seed of heaven, increasing with milk; we implore him for his favor and for wide-reaching protection.
He who is the pillar of heaven, its support, well-spread—the Soma-stalk that flows full from every side;
he, the sage, has sustained these two great worlds, heaven and earth, with their alternating turns, and has held them together as they meet, along with all strengthening foods.
Great is the food, well-prepared, sweet with Soma; wide is the pasture for the one who follows the Law of Aditi.
He who rules over the rain from here, the ruddy bull, the leader of the waters, he who is worthy of praise and whose aid is near;
The watery cloud, possessing breath, is milked for ghee and milk; the navel of Cosmic Order, immortality, is born.
United, the bounteous ones, those men, the overflowing ones, delight him and pour out what is beneficial like a stream.
The ray has roared, accompanied by its wave; it swells the skin that is dear to the gods for the sake of man.
It places the germ in the lap of Aditi, by which we may obtain both offspring and descendants. May those unfailing streams, rich in progeny, flow down in a thousand streams into the third realm.
Four navels are established below the sky; they bring the immortal oblation, dripping with clarified butter.

Soma assumes a white form when he desires to win; the bountiful Asura knows the full extent of the world. He accompanies the prayer and the ritual labor; may he burst open the water-bearing cask from heaven.

Then the white vessel, anointed with milk, has stepped forward to its place, having won the prize. The seekers of the gods have sent forth with their minds a gift of cattle for Kakṣīvat, who has lived a hundred winters.
O Soma, as your juice mingles with the waters, it flows through the sheep’s wool while you are being purified.
Being cleansed by the poets, O most exhilarating one, be sweet for Indra’s drinking, O Pavamāna.
Well-disposed toward his dear names, the mighty one flows forth, he upon whom he grows strong.
Great and far-seeing, he has mounted the wide-reaching chariot of the great Sūrya.
The tongue of *Ṛta* flows forth as the beloved honey; the inviolable lord of this prayer speaks. As a son, he bestows upon his parents their secret third name in the luminous realm of heaven.
Shining down, he has roared toward the jars, guided by men into the golden vessel.
They have sung praises to him, the milker of Truth; he, the three-backed one, shines forth over the dawns.
Pressed by the stones and prepared by the hymns, the pure one, illuminating the two parents, Heaven and Earth, flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece, swelling with streams of honey day after day.
O Soma, flow forth for our well-being; being purified by the men, clothe yourself in the milk-mixture.
With those exhilarating, far-reaching intoxications of yours, impel Indra to grant us wealth.
The sustainer of heaven, the effective juice, the skillful power of the gods, flows clear, to be celebrated by the men.

Like a tawny steed released by warriors, he effortlessly displays his splendors in the rivers. Like a hero, he takes weapons in his hands, desiring to win the light of heaven as a charioteer in the quest for cattle.
Stirring up the vigor of Indra with his labors, the drop, being urged forward, is anointed by the wise.
O Soma Pavamāna, entering the bellies of Indra with your wave, manifesting your power;
swell for us like lightning in the cloud, filling both worlds, and through our prayer, measure out for us eternal strengths.
The King of all, who beholds the light of heaven, flows clear; conquering the seers, he has caused the thought of *Ṛta* to resound.
He who is cleansed by the ray of the sun, the father of hymns, whose wisdom is peerless;
like a bull toward the herds, you flow into the vat, a bellowing steer in the lap of the waters.
You flow for Indra as the most intoxicating one, so that with your aid we may conquer in the encounter.
This honeyed one has roared forward into the vat, Indra’s thunderbolt, more wondrous than the wondrous;
toward him flow the well-milking, ghee-dropping streams of Truth, like lowing cows with their milk.
He, the ancient one, flows clear, whom the falcon, dispatched from heaven, churned forth across the mid-air.
He, trembling, draws the honeyed juice, fearing in his mind before the swift Kṛśānu.
May those ancient and later drops of Soma flow for us toward great wealth consisting of cattle—
those who are beautiful to behold like serpents, and who have delighted in every prayer and every oblation.
May this Indu, the wise one praised by many with a focused mind, conquer those who attack us.
He who has placed the germ in the seat of the Mighty One flows toward the wide-opening stall of the cattle.
The active, effectual juice of heaven flows clear; great and undeceived, he is called Varuṇa, the one who goes across the waters.
Mitra, worthy of sacrifice, has been pressed out for the clans, bellowing like a stallion eager for the herd among the flocks.
The King, generating the voice, has flowed forth; clothed in the waters, he strives to win the cows. He seizes the impurity within his body; purified, he goes to the appointed place of the gods.

O Soma, you are poured out for Indra by the men; you, the seer with the gaze of a hero, are anointed as a wave in the wood. For many are your paths to travel, and a thousand bay horses, seated in the vessels, attend upon you.
The Apsarases of the ocean have flowed toward the wise one, the Soma, as he sat within.
They urge him on, the conqueror of the stronghold; they beg for favor from the imperishable Pavamāna.
Winning cattle for us, winning chariots, winning gold, winning the light, winning unassailable wealth, winning thousands—Soma flows clear.
Him whom the gods have made into a gladdening draught for drinking, the sweetest drop, ruddy and source of bliss.
O Soma Pavamāna, seeking us, making these true riches manifest, you flow onward.
Slay the enemy both near and far; grant us wide pastures and security.
May our unurged drops, the tawny ones, flow forth when pressed among those of lofty heaven.
May our enemies perish; may the hostilities of the enemy perish. May our prayers attain their goal and win us wealth.
Let the Soma drops flow forth for us, distilling exhilaration—the very riches for which we urge on our horses.
Beyond the encompassing reach of any mortal whatsoever, may we carry away all manner of treasures.
Indeed, he is an enemy through his own ill-will, for he is a wolf through the ill-will of another.
Like thirst in the desert, O Soma Pavamāna, strike down those of evil intent.
Your highest navel is in heaven, where it was taken up; your shoots have grown upon the ridges of the earth.
The pressing-stones devour you upon the ox-hide; the wise ones have milked you from the waters with their hands.
Thus, O Indu, do the first adornments force forth your well-formed, beautiful, and splendid juice.
O Pavamāna, drive away every reproach; let your fervor be manifest, a beloved exhilaration.

The stream of Soma, who beholds men, flows clear; by the Eternal Law, he calls the gods from heaven. O Bṛhaspati, he has flashed forth with thundering roar; like oceans, the libations have expanded to contain him.
O vigorous one, you whom the cows have greeted with lowing, you ascend your iron-fashioned womb, radiant and glorious.
Prolonging the life of the patrons and bringing great renown, flow, O Soma, as a bull-like exhilaration for Indra.
Flowing most intoxicatingly into the belly of Indra, clothing yourself in strength, you, the most auspicious one, flow for the sake of glory.
He has spread himself out toward all beings; playing, the golden-hued steed, the bull, flows onward.
The ten fingers milk you, O man, for the sake of the gods—the most honey-sweet one with a thousand streams.
O Soma, set in motion by men and pressed by the stones, flow pure for all the gods as a conqueror of thousands.
The ten fingers, like those with hands, milk you, the honey-sweet bull, into the waters with the pressing-stones.
RV 9.80.5: O Soma, exhilarating Indra and the divine host, you flow as Pavamāna like a wave from the ocean.
RV 9.81.1: The well-adorned waves of the purifying Soma go forth into the belly of Indra.
RV 9.81.2: When the pressed juices, mixed with curds and the glorious milk of cows, have been drawn up, they have gladdened the Hero for the giving of gifts.
For Soma has flowed toward the jars like a draft-horse, a stallion with swift-moving tracks.
Thus, knowing both races of the gods, he reaches that which is here and that which is beyond.
O Soma Pavamāna, scatter wealth upon us; O Indu, be a bountiful lord of great riches.
Bestow strength upon the Vasu with your wise insight; do not pour away our household wealth from us. May Pūṣan, Pavamāna, the liberal Mitra, and Varuṇa come to us in harmony;
may Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Vāyu, the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, and the well-guided Sarasvatī come as well.
Both Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading ones; the god Aryaman, Aditi, and the Ordainer;
Bhaga, the one who looks upon men, and the wide mid-air—all the gods have taken pleasure in Pavamāna.
The tawny Soma has been pressed, the red bull; like a wondrous king, he has bellowed toward the cows.

Being purified, he goes around the unwoven fleece to sit upon it like a hawk in his nest, as if upon a place rich in ghee. As a sage, you go around with the skill of a priest; like a groomed steed, you rush toward the prize.
Driving away misfortunes, O Soma, be gracious; clothed in ghee, you go around to your bright garment.
Parjanya is the father of the great-winged bird; he has established his dwelling upon the mountains at the navel of the earth.

The sisterly waters have flowed toward the cows, and he meets with the pressing-stones when the sacrifice is desired. Like a wife for her husband, O gracious one, you bestow favor; O child of Pajrā, hear me, for I speak to you.
Enter among the inner songs that we may live well; blameless, O Soma, keep watch within the community.
Just as for the ancients you went forth, O Indu, winning hundreds and thousands of spoils without fail, so now flow clear for new prosperity; the waters follow according to your law.
RV 9.83.1: Your filter is stretched out, O Brahmaṇaspati; as the Lord, you encompass its limbs from every side.

He whose body has not been heated by penance, being raw, does not partake of that [soma]; only those who have been cooked [by fire] and carry it reach it together. The filter of heat is stretched out at the station of heaven; its glowing threads have spread abroad.
The swift ones protect his filter; with their mind, they mount the back of heaven.
The foremost dappled bull has caused the dawns to shine; seeking strength, he sustains all beings.
By his creative power, the masters of illusion have measured it out; the fathers, who behold men, have placed the embryo within him.
The Gandharva thus guards his station; the wonderful one protects the generations of the gods.
As the lord of the treasure, he seizes the enemy with his snare; those who do most good have partaken of the draught of honey.
O possessor of oblations, clothed in the great divine dwelling-place and the mist, you shall go around the sacrifice as the sacrificial offering.
RV 9.83.5: O King, whose chariot is the filter, who mounts for booty, with a thousand points, you conquer lofty renown.
RV 9.84.1: Flow on, exhilarating the gods, far-seeing, winning the waters, for Indra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu.
RV 9.84.2: Create for us today wide space and well-being; dwell in broad habitations and praise the divine host.
The immortal Soma, who has taken his stand over all the worlds, flows around them; effecting both gathering and dispersal for our aid, Indu follows after the Dawn as the Sun does.
He who is poured out with milk among the plants, seeking the favor of the gods, approaches us bringing wealth.
With a flash of lightning, the pressed Soma flows in a stream, exhilarating Indra and the divine host.
This very Soma, the winner of thousands, flows on, inspiring the vigorous voice that awakens at dawn.
Indu sends the ocean surging with the winds; he settles within the jars, the heart of Indra.
The cows mix that Soma with milk—him who increases the milk—with their prayers; he is the finder of heaven.
The wealth-conquering, effective juice flows clear; the inspired sage, a seer through his poetic wisdom, shines with celestial light.
O Soma, well-pressed for Indra, flow around; let disease be driven away along with the demons.
Let not the double-dealing ones revel in your juice; let the drops here be possessed of wealth.

O Pavamāna, urge us forward in the battle; for you are the skillful, beloved exhilaration of the gods. Strike down the enemies who raise their voices in derision; drink the Soma, O Indra, and drive away our foes.
O Indu, unassailable and most exhilarating, you flow clear; you become the supreme nourishment for Indra’s self. Many wise ones sing toward you; they honor the king of this world as its foundation.
With a thousand paths and a hundred streams, the wondrous Indu flows clear as desirable honey for Indra.
Winning the field, flow hither; winning the waters, O bounteous Soma, make wide for us a path to go.
Bellowing loudly, you are anointed with milk in the jar; you pass through the middle of the woolly filter. Being cleansed like a prize-winning steed, O Soma, you have flowed into the belly of Indra.
Flow sweet for the celestial race; flow sweet for Indra, whose name is easily invoked. Flow sweet, honeyed, and inviolable for Mitra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati.
The ten fingers cleanse the steed in the jar; the inspired thoughts and voices of the sages surge forth.
The purifying drops flow toward the beautiful hymn; the intoxicating *indus* enter Indra.
Purifying himself, flow toward us with heroic strength, a wide pasture, and great, far-reaching protection.
Let no one have power over this our outpouring; O *indu*, may we win wealth after wealth through you.
The far-seeing bull has mounted the sky; the sage has illuminated the luminous realms of heaven.
The King passes through the filter with a roar; those who watch over men milk the nectar of heaven.
On the vault of heaven, the honey-tongued, unceasing seers milk the mountain-dwelling bull.

The drop that has grown great in the waters, in the ocean, in the wave of the river, within the filter— To the eagle who has flown up to the firmament, the many songs of the longing ones have cried out.
The prayers lick the infant, the one worthy of praise, the golden bird standing upon the earth.
The Gandharva has stood erect upon the firmament, beholding all the forms of this [universe].
His radiance has shone forth with bright luster; pure, he has illuminated both worlds, the two parents.
O Pavamāna, your swift, exhilarating drops, urged by the prayer, flow forth of their own accord like those born of fleet steeds.
The divine, well-winged drops, honey-sweet and most intoxicating, settle around the vessel.
Your exhilarating, swift draughts have been poured forth separately, like chariot-horses.
Like a cow with milk for her calf, the honeyed waves of soma-drops flow toward Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Like a steed urged forward, he rushes toward the prize, seeking the light, the vessel of heaven whose mother is the rock.
As a bull upon the back of the sheep’s-wool filter, Soma, being purified, flows for the sake of Indra’s nourishment.
O Pavamāna, your heavenly, thought-swift, Ashvin-like streams have been released with their milk to support the cosmic order.
The ancient seers have poured forth the aged [streams]—those wise ones who, O you who are the steed of the seers, cleanse you.
Your rays, O all-seeing and skillful Lord, encompass all domains as you exist.
Pervading with your laws, O Soma, you flow clear; as the Lord of the entire world, you reign supreme.
On both sides the rays of Pavamāna, who is steadfast, go forth as his banners;
when the tawny one is cleansed upon the filter, he sits down in his place within the jars.
As the banner of the sacrifice, the well-performing Soma flows; he goes to the appointed place of the gods.
Flowing in a thousand streams, he rushes around the vat; the bull, bellowing loudly, passes through the filter.
The King plunges into the ocean and the rivers; resting in the streams, he unites with the wave of the waters.
Pavamāna has mounted the back of the sheep’s wool; he is the supporter of the great heaven at the navel of the earth.
Like the ridge of heaven, he has thundered and roared—he whose laws both heaven and earth obey.
Purifying himself and finding the friendship of Indra, Soma flows and settles within the jars.
The light of the sacrifice, the beloved honey, flows clear; he is the father of the gods, their progenitor, the possessor of abundant wealth.
The most intoxicating, exhilarating, and Indra-like juice bestows a treasure hidden within the two self-sustaining worlds.
Roaring toward the jar, the prize-winning steed flows in a hundred streams, the far-seeing lord of heaven.
Tawny-hued, he settles in the dwelling places of Mitra, being cleansed by the sheep’s wool and the waters, the bull.
Pavamāna flows at the head of the rivers; as the foremost one, he goes at the head of speech toward the cattle.
He shares in the great prize of booty at the head; well-armed, the bull is purified by the pressers.
Like a bird sent forth, this Pavamāna, full of thought, has flowed with his wave into the sheep’s wool.
By your power, O Sage, the pure Soma flows between the two worlds, heaven and earth, through your inspired thought for you, O Indra.

Clothed in his mantle, the worshipful one reaches to heaven; filling the mid-air, he is established among all beings. Born from the light, he has stepped forth with the mist; he seeks to win over his ancient father.
He bestows great protection upon that person who has attained his first abode;
from that station of his which is in the highest heaven, he comes together with all things in full control.
The drop has gone forth to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not violate the agreement of his friend.

Like a youth with young women, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred courses. Your thoughts, joyous, praising, and worthy of honor, have stepped forth into the dwellings. The inspired hymns have celebrated Soma; the milch-cows have poured their milk upon him.
O Soma, as you flow clear, O Indu, pour forth for us abundant and swelling food,

an unfailing stream that yields for us thrice daily— food rich in cattle, strength, sweetness, and heroic power. The bull of our hymns, the far-seeing Soma, flows on, the furtherer of the day, the dawn, and the sky.
Flowing forth, he has caused the jars of the rivers to resound, entering the heart of Indra with the wise.
With the wise, the ancient sage flows clear; guided by men, he has roared around the vessels.
Generating the name of Trita, let him pour forth sweetness so that Indra and Vāyu may form friendship.

This one, being purified, has caused the dawns to shine; this one has become the maker of space for the rivers. This Soma, milking the thrice-seven [cows] for the milk-mixture, flows as a delightful intoxicant for the heart.
Flow on, O Soma, in your celestial abodes; being released, O Indu, flow through the filter into the jar.
Sitting within the belly of Indra, bellowing loudly, directed by the men, you caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Pressed by the stones, you flow through the filter, O Indu, entering the bellies of Indra.
You became the one who watches over men, O far-seeing Soma; you opened the cow-pen for the Aṅgirases.
O Soma, while you are being purified, the wise sages, seeking aid, have rejoiced in you with their well-practiced hymns.

The fair-winged eagle brought you down from heaven, O Indu, you who are adorned by all our prayers. As you, the tawny one, are purified in the fleece with your wave through the filter, the seven milch-cows low toward you.
In the lap of the waters, the eager ones have impelled the Sage toward the womb of Cosmic Order; like mighty bulls, they have urged him on.
Being purified, Indu plunges through all adversaries, making every path easy for the sacrificer.
Making the cows his mantle, the lovely Sage, like a playful horse, flows around the fleece.
The ceaseless, hundred-streamed, glorious waters cry out to the golden one, like those seeking water;
they cleanse him who is enveloped in milk upon the third ridge, in the luminous realm of heaven.
These creatures of yours are born of divine seed; you rule over the entire world.
Now this entire universe is under your control, O Pavamāna; you, O Indu, were the first to establish the foundations.
You are the ocean, O Sage who knows all; these five directions are within your sustaining power.
You have extended beyond both heaven and earth; yours are the lights, O Pavamāna, and Sūrya himself.
O Soma Pavamāna, you are purified in the filter for the gods within the expanse of the mid-world.
The first seekers grasped you; all these worlds have submitted themselves to you.
The singer goes forth across the sheep’s wool filter; the tawny bull bellows down upon the wooden vessels.
The prayers have lowed together in longing; the hymns lick the infant who is worthy of praise.
He has clothed himself in the rays of the sun, weaving the threefold thread as he knows how.
Leading the newest instructions of the sacred law, the husband of the women goes to the appointed place.
The king of rivers flows on, the lord of heaven; he goes along the paths of *ṛta*, bellowing loudly.
With a thousand streams the golden-hued one is poured out; being purified, generating speech, he approaches with wealth.
O Pavamāna, like a wondrous sun, you flow through the sheep’s woolly filter as a great flood.
Purified by the hands, pressed by the men with stones, you flow for great and prize-winning booty.
O Pavamāna, you rush toward nourishment and vigor; like a falcon, you settle in the wooden vessels.
Pressed as a gladdening draught for Indra, you are the supreme exhilarating drink, the pillar of heaven, far-seeing.
The seven sisters, the mothers, attend upon the newborn infant, the noble and wise one.
The celestial Gandharva of the waters, who beholds men—Soma—is for the sovereignty over the entire world. As Lord, you traverse these worlds, O Indu, having yoked your tawny, well-winged mares.
May these [streams] flow for you with honeyed ghee and milk; O Soma, may the people abide in your service.
O Soma Pavamāna, you are the beholder of men from every side; O Bull, you run through them all.
As such, flow for us with wealth and gold; may we be among living beings that we might live.
Flow on, finding cattle, finding wealth, finding gold, O Indu, bestowing seed, established among all beings.
O Soma, you are a hero of noble strength and the knower of all; as such, the sages sit near you with their songs of praise.
The wave of honey has caused the woods to stand; clothed in waters, the buffalo plunges deep.
The King, whose chariot is the filter, has mounted for the prize; with a thousand points, he wins great renown.
He raises up all the blessed songs rich in progeny, bringing them day by day, O All-Living One, well-supported.
O Indu, once drunk, do thou entreat Indra on our behalf for a prayer that brings offspring and wealth abounding in horses.
At the beginning of days, the golden, desirable exhilaration is made conscious by the wise one through the following days.
Driving the two peoples apart, he moves between them—the men and the divine praise—while upholding the law.
They anoint him, they smear him, they anoint him all over; they lick his power and anoint him with honey.
At the swelling of the river, they who purify with gold seize the bull as he falls into the waters; they grasp him among the cattle.
Sing forth to the wise Pavamāna! Like a great stream, the Soma-juice flows onward.
Like a serpent gliding over its slough, like a playful horse, the tawny bull has sped forth.
The leader, the king, the measurer of days, established among the worlds, shall be praised.
Tawny, dripping with clarity, beautiful to behold, a surging ocean, whose chariot is light—he flows as the one who dwells in wealth.
The supporting pillar of heaven has been released; the exhilarating draught, threefold in nature, flows around all the worlds.

The hymns lick the stalk that merits praise, when those who sing the *ṛc* have approached his radiant garment with song. Your streams, as you are being purified, flow forth like swift rams through the fine woolen filter.
When, O Indu, you are mixed with milk in the two bowls, you, O Soma, being pressed, settle within the jars.
Flow on, O Soma, winner of wisdom, worthy of our hymns; run through the sheep’s wool, pouring out your beloved honey.
Slay all the demons and devourers, O Indu! May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Run forth toward the vessel and settle therein; being purified by the men, flow toward the prize of victory.
Grooming you like a prize-winning horse, they lead you toward the sacred grass with reins.
The well-armed divine Soma flows, the slayer of the accursed, protecting the community.
Father of the gods, their progenitor, most skillful, he is the pillar of heaven and the support of the earth.
The seer, the sage, the leader of the people, the skillful and wise Uśanas through his poetic insight—
he indeed discovered that secret, hidden name of the cows which was cherished by them.
This honeyed, bull-like Soma of yours, O Indra, has flowed for you, the bull, through the filter.
Winning thousands, winning hundreds, a bountiful giver, the prize-winner has taken his place upon the sacrificial grass for all time.
These Soma drops have been poured forth through the filters toward cattle-wealth, toward great strength, and toward immortality and glory.
Purifying themselves with the filters, they have flowed like fame-seeking steeds rushing to battle.
For he, invoked by many, being purified, has indeed flowed around all the nourishments of the people.
Now, O you who are borne by the falcon, bring us refreshments; bestowing wealth, flow toward booty.
This Soma, being pressed, has run through the filter like a released herd of horses.

Whetting his sharp horns like a bull, he rushes toward the cows like a hero seeking cattle. This one has come from the innermost depth of the distant mountain; finding them somewhere in the wide expanse, she has discovered the cows.
Like lightning from heaven thundering with clouds, O Indra, your stream of Soma flows clear.
And indeed, O Soma, being purified, you go around the heap of cattle on the same chariot with Indra.
O you who give life swiftly, grant us many great refreshments; those are yours, O powerful one, for which you are praised.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; for you it flows clear; drink of this!

You indeed have drawn it forth; you have poured out the drop, the Soma, for the fitting exhilaration. Like a chariot that wins much, he has been harnessed; the great one [has been yoked] for the winning of many riches.
Then all the human races, at the winning of the light, cried out to the upright tree.
Like Vāyu with his teams of horses, you who are most beneficent when invoked like the Nāsatyas;
you are all-desirable, like Draviṇodas in person, and like Pūṣan, O Soma, you are the impeller of our thoughts.
Like Indra, you who have performed great deeds, you are the slayer of Vṛtras and the shatterer of forts, O Soma.
For like a horse, O Soma, you are the slayer of every Dasyu among those called "serpents.
Like Agni when released into the forest, he displays his powers at will within the rivers.
Like a warrior, the roaring host, Soma Pavamāna sends forth his wave with a great clamor.
These Soma juices have flowed through the sheep’s wool filter like celestial water-jars raining from the clouds;
like rivers flowing easily downward to the ocean, the pressed drops have been poured into the jars.
Flow on, O powerful one, like the host of Maruts, as one who is beyond reproach, even as the divine folk.
RV 9.88.7: May your favor come to us quickly like water; may it be like a sacrifice that wins thousands and conquers armies.
RV 9.88.8: Now, your laws are indeed those of King Varuṇa...
RV 9.89.1: This carrier has sped forth along his paths; Pavamāna has flowed like rain from heaven.
In a thousand streams Soma has settled among us, in the lap of his mother, and in the wood. The King of rivers has clothed himself in his garment; he has mounted the straightest ship of *ṛta*.
The drop has grown strong in the waters, urged by the falcon; the father milks it, and he milks the offspring of the father.
They bring the lion toward us—the tireless one, the honey-sweet, the tawny, the ruddy lord of this heaven.
The hero, foremost in battles, seeks the cattle; the bull protects them all around with his eye.
They harness to the chariot the horse whose back is honeyed, the terrible, the tireless, the wide-wheeled and lofty steed.
The sisters, his female kin, cleanse him; those of common origin strengthen the prize-winner. Four milch-cows yielding ghee attend him, seated together within the same supporting vessel.
Purifying themselves, they flow toward him with reverence; these many ones encompass him from every side.
The pillar of heaven, the supporter of earth, and all the settlements of men are in his hand.

May there be for you a spring for the singer, O Lord of the teams; may the stalk of honey flow for Indra’s power. Winning [the prize], unassailed, flow for the feast of the gods; O Soma, as the slayer of Vṛtra, flow for Indra.

Grant us great wealth, most resplendent; may we be masters of heroic power. Urged forward, the progenitor of heaven and earth has gone forth like a chariot seeking booty, approaching Indra, sharpening his weapons, and taking all treasures into his hands.
The voices have cried out toward the three-backed bull, the bestower of vital strength, with songs of praise.
Enveloping himself in the woods like Varuṇa among the rivers, the bestower of jewels distributes desirable treasures.
As one whose host is heroic, possessing all warriors, victorious, and a winner of wealth, flow on, O Pavamāna.
Armed with sharp weapons and a swift bow, unconquered in battles, he overcomes his enemies in the fray.
Creating wide pastures and security, flow toward us, O Soma, bringing together the two worlds and the abundance of wisdom.
Striving to win the waters, the dawns, and the heavenly realms, roar forth and bestow upon us great spoils of war.
O Soma, exhilarate Varuṇa; exhilarate Mitra; O Indu, as you flow clear, exhilarate Indra and Viṣṇu.
Exhilarate the host of Maruts; exhilarate the gods; O Indu, exhilarate the great Indra for his intoxication.
Thus, like a king measuring out his will, flow on, striking down all misfortunes.
O Indu, bestow vital strength for our well-spoken hymn; and do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Like a steed let loose for a chariot-race, the first inspired thinker, the visionary, has been set free by prayer.
The ten sisters drive the bearer upon the sheep’s back toward his seats.
Pressed by the sons of Nahuṣa, along with the wisdom of the divine folk, Indu flows forth for the feast.
He who is immortal, being cleansed by mortal men— with the sheep’s wool, with milk,
and with waters— The bull, bellowing loudly for the Bull, this Pavamāna, as the bright drop, stirs up the white milk of the cow.
The hymn-singing Sun, the knower of speech, traverses the narrow path by a thousand ways that are free from dust.
O Indu, as you are being purified, shatter even the firm dwellings of the demons; open up the paths to booty for us.
Strike down with your swift weapon those who are near and those who are far, so that they may be brought low.

As in the past, O possessor of all boons, prepare the forward paths for our newest hymn of praise. May we attain those great [powers] which are difficult for the enemy to overcome, O performer of many deeds, O provider of much food!
Thus being purified, grant us the waters, the heavenly realms, and abundant offspring and descendants.
RV 9.91.6: O Soma, grant us prosperity for our wide field and light; grant us the sun so that we may behold it. RV 9.92.1:
The tawny stalk, being pressed, has been released into the filter like a chariot urged forward for the sake of gain.
RV 9.92.2: Being purified, he has attained fame and Indra-like power; he has gratified the gods with his offerings.

Beholding men, he has flowed toward the filter, assuming his name; as a seer, he settles in his own womb. Sitting in the vessels like a Hotṛ-priest in his seat, the seven inspired Ṛṣis have approached him.
Soma, the wise one who knows the way and belongs to all the gods, goes to his eternal seat while being purified.
He becomes the one who delights in all poetic insights; the wise one exerts himself among the five peoples.
O Soma Pavamāna, in your secret place are all those gods, the thirty-three.
By their own powers, the ten [fingers] and the seven mighty rivers cleanse you upon the sheep’s back.
May that indeed be the truth of Pavamāna, wherein all the poets gather together.
Since he created light for the day and made room for the world, he protected Manu from the Dasyu who was a source of distress.
Like a Hotṛ priest passing by enclosures rich in cattle, like a true king proceeding to assemblies.
Soma, being purified, has gone to the jars, settling like a wild buffalo in the forests.
The ten sisters, the flowing prayers of the sage, have cleansed him together with their moisture.
The tawny one, born of the Sun, has run around and reached the vat like a prize-winning steed.

Like a crying infant with its mothers, the bull, possessing many treasures, has flowed forth with the waters. Like a youth going to a maiden at the appointed place, he unites in the jar with the milk-cows.
And the udder of the cow has swelled; the wise drop accompanies her with its streams.
The cows mix the head [of Soma] with milk in the vessels, as if with purified treasures.
O Indu, being purified, do thou, yearning for us, bestow upon us wealth consisting of horses along with the gods.
May Purandhi, the charioteer-like one who desires us, come toward us to grant riches.
Now, being purified, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroes, all-glittering and worthy of being protected by the wind.
O Indu, may the life-span of the singer be extended; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
When beauty vies for him as for a prize-winning steed, the prayers of the people strive toward him like rays toward the sun.
Choosing the waters, he flows as one seeking the seer’s vision; like a pen for the increase of cattle, he stirs the prayer.
Twofold unfolding the abode of immortality, the worlds expand for the finding of the light of heaven.
Like cows swelling with milk in the stall, the prayers longing for the Truth low toward Indu.
When the sage bears his poetic wisdom around all the worlds like a hero in a chariot, he provides glory for mortals among the gods—new wealth for skillful men, abounding in many forms.
Born for splendor, he has come forth from splendor; he bestows splendor and vital strength upon those who praise him.
Clothed in glory, they have attained immortality; their encounters become true when the course is measured.
Flow toward us with nourishment and vigor, toward horses and cattle; create wide light and exhilarate the gods.
For all those things are easily overcome by you; O Soma Pavamāna, you drive away our enemies.
The tawny one neighs loudly as he is let loose, settling within the belly of the wooden vessel while being purified.
Guided by the men, he makes the cow his garment; from there, through his inherent powers, he generates inspired thoughts.
The tawny one, released upon the path of Truth, sends forth his voice like a boat across the waters.
The god makes manifest the secret names of the gods upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) so that they may be proclaimed.
Like the surging waves of the waters, our inspired thoughts (*manīṣā*) hasten toward Soma. Paying homage, they approach him and enter into him, longing for him who longs for them.
They milk that Soma-stalk, the bellowing bull dwelling on the mountain, as one cleanses him upon the ridge like a wild beast.
To him, as he bellows, the prayers cling; Trita sustains Varuṇa within the ocean.
Sending forth your voice like the Upavaktṛ priest of the Hotṛ, O Indu, being purified, release your inspired thought.
And when you two, Indra and [Agni], dwell together for our good fortune, may we be masters of great heroic power.
The hero, the leader of the chariots, goes at the head of the hosts seeking cattle; his army exults.
Making the invocations of Indra auspicious for his friends, Soma puts on his impetuous garments.
The bay steeds groom his bay horse with unceasing praises, sharpening him like horses with their homage.
As the friend of Indra, he mounts the chariot; knowing the way, he goes toward the gracious favor.
O God, flow for us through the service of the gods, O Soma, as food for the great Indra-drinking.
Making the waters flow and raining down upon this broad heaven, purifying yourself, grant us wide space.
Flow on for the sake of non-defeat, for non-slaughter, for well-being, and for great, complete prosperity.
All these friends desire that; O Soma Pavamāna, I too desire that.
Soma flows clear, the progenitor of hymns, the progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth;
the progenitor of Agni, the progenitor of Sūrya, the progenitor of Indra, and the progenitor of Viṣṇu.
He is the Brahman of the gods, the leader of the poets, the seer of the sages, and the buffalo among wild beasts.
Like a hawk among vultures, like an axe among the forests, Soma goes singing across the filter.
Soma Pavamāna has caused the wave of speech, the songs, and the inspired thoughts to flow forth like a river.
Beholding these lower realms within, he stands as a bull among the cows, knowing them well.
May he, the exhilarating one, winning in battles, unassailed, with thousandfold seed, flow toward booty.
O Indu, as you purify yourself for Indra, being wise, send forth the wave of the stalk, impelling the cows.
The beloved Soma, desired by the gods, flows around into the jar for Indra, delightful for his exhilaration.
With a thousand streams and a hundredfold strength, the Soma-drop, like a prize-winning steed, goes to the assembly.
Being born as the ancient winner of wealth, cleansed in the waters and pressed by the stones,
the protector from curses and king of the world, he provides a path for the prayer while being purified.
For by you, O Soma, our ancient fathers performed their sacred rites, O Pavamāna, they who were wise.

Conquering the unassailable, open up the enclosures; be a bountiful lord to us with heroes and horses. Just as you have flowed for Manu, bestowing vital strength, slaying enemies, finding wide space, and accompanied by oblations.
Flow on thus, bestowing wealth; unite with Indra and bring forth your weapons.
Flow on, O Soma, honey-sweet and true to the Law, clothing yourself in waters upon the sheep’s-wool back.
Settle down in the wooden vats that are full of ghee—most gladdening, intoxicating, and the drink of Indra.
Flow with a hundred streams from heaven for rain, winning a thousandfold at the feast of the gods, seeking booty.
Bellowing together with the rivers in the jar, and with the milk-streams, prolong our life.
This very Soma, being purified by hymns, like a prize-winning steed, overcomes hostilities.
Like fresh milk drawn from Aditi, like a wide path easy to traverse, you are led forth by the pressers.
Purified by the pressers, O God Soma, flow toward your secret and beautiful name; as a steed for the sake of glory, flow toward booty, toward Vāyu, and toward the cows.
They cleanse the beloved infant as soon as he is born; the Maruts with their host adorn him, the bearer of the sacrifice.
As a seer through his songs and as a sage through his wisdom, Soma goes singing across the filter.
He whose mind is that of a rishi, who creates rishis, who wins the light of heaven, who leads a thousand ways—he is the pathfinder of the sages.

Desiring to attain his third station, the mighty Soma shines as the sovereign king over the Virāj. Sitting in the vessels like a hawk, a far-reaching bird, the drop that finds the cattle bears its weapons.
Following the wave of the waters toward the ocean, the mighty one proclaims his fourth station.
Like a handsome youth adorning his body, like a courser who has run for the winning of riches; like a bull rushing toward the herds, he flows into the vat, bellowing as he enters the two bowls.
Flow on, O Indu, as the purifying one with your great powers; bellowing, flow around the woolen filters.
Playing, enter our two [bowls] while being purified; let your exhilarating juice intoxicate Indra.
His great streams have been released; anointed with milk, he has entered the jars.
Creating the *sāman*, the wise singer approaches, crying out like a friend toward his kin.
Striking down the enemies, O Pavamāna, you go forth like a lover singing to his beloved; Indu flows on.
Like a bird flying to its nest, Soma, being purified, settles within the jars.
Your splendors, O Pavamāna Soma, come like a woman—well-yielding, with excellent streams.
The golden-hued one, rich in boons, has been brought; he has bellowed within the waters of the vessels of the god-seeking ones.
Being purified by his impulse and his impetus, the god has mingled his juice with the gods.
Pressed, he goes around the filter chanting like a Hotar-priest at measured stations rich in cattle.
Clothed in auspicious garments, together with his companions, the great seer pronounces the sacred words.
Flowing toward the two bowls while being purified, far-seeing and watchful at the feast for the gods.
On the sheep’s back, the beloved one is cleansed, most glorious among the glorious, our protector.
Resound as you flow, being purified; do you protect us always with your blessings.
Sing forth! Let us worship the gods; send forth Soma for the sake of great wealth.
Sweet, he flows through the sheep’s wool filter; like one desiring our gods, he shall sit within the jar.
The drop, approaching the friendship of the gods, flows in a thousand streams for exhilaration.
Praised by men according to the ancient ordinance, he has gone to Indra for great good fortune.
Flowing gold-hued for the sake of wealth, O Soma, as you are purified, let your exhilarating juice go to Indra for his support.
Come on the same chariot with the gods toward the gift; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Proclaiming poetic wisdom like Uśanas, the god declares the generations of the gods.
Of great vows, pure kinsman, and purifier, he approaches the stations bellowing like a wild boar.
The swans have driven away the impetuous fury; the bull-like hosts have gone home.

O friends, they together sound the song for the praiseworthy Pavamāna, which is impossible to withstand. He hastens with the speed of the wide-striding one; like cows lowing, they measure out him who sports at will.
The sharp-horned one makes himself full; by day he appears as a bay horse, by night as a dappled steed.
The vigorous Soma, the drop, flows through the cow-stall; the Soma goes to Indra, inciting him to exhilaration.
He slays the demon and drives away the enemies; creating wide space, he is the king of the community.
Then, mingled with sweetness in a stream, milked by the stones, he flows through the wool;
the drop, enjoying the friendship of Indra, the exhilarating god, flows for the intoxication of the god.
Purifying himself, the god flows toward his dear ones, mingling the gods with his own juice.
The drop, clothing itself in its functions according to the seasons, has clothed itself upon the woolly summit among the ten fingers.
Like a red bull bellowing toward the cows, he goes, making both earth and heaven resound.
Like the roar of Indra, his cry is heard in the battle; making this voice known, he flows onward.
Worthy of being tasted, swelling with milk, you go forth impelling the honeyed stalk.
O Soma, as you are purified and poured out for Indra, you go making a continuous sound.
Flow on thus, intoxicating for exhilaration, bending down the weapons of the one who seizes from on high.
Bearing your radiant color all around, O Soma, flow for us as one seeking cattle, being poured out.
O Indu, having found pleasure in us, flow on easy paths and fair ways, creating wide spaces for our prosperity.
Striking away misfortunes on every side like a club, run over the high ridge upon the sheep’s wool.
Send down for us the rain from heaven that comes swiftly, full of nourishment, bringing health and quickening gifts.
Like a loosened lock of hair, O Indu, flow along the desert, distinguishing these lower kinsmen and the winds.
Purifying yourself, O Soma, untie the knotted tangle, and distinguish between the straight path and the crooked way.
Like a steed, the tawny one neighs as he is let loose; O God, run like a youth who dwells in the house.
O Indu, beloved for the exhilaration of the gods, flow with your swelling mass over the back of the sheep’s wool.
Flowing in a thousand streams, fragrant and inviolable, pour yourself out for the winning of booty in the battle of men.
Those which are without reins, without chariots, unyoked, like horses let loose in the race—these bright Soma drops flow; O gods, come near to them to drink!
Thus, O Indu, flow for us toward the feast of the gods; flow like a cloud, a flood, into the vessels.
May Soma grant us desirable, vast wealth, accompanied by heroic sons and formidable power.

When the speech of the longing mind fashioned him, or when, under the law of the Eldest, he stood at the surface of the milk; then the cows, lowing toward their choice, came to Indu in the jar as their beloved lord.
The celestial giver, swelling with gifts, flows forward; the wise one purifies the *ṛta* for the sake of *ṛta*.
He becomes the upholder of the law, the king of the assembly; he is borne across the earth by his ten rays.
Purifying himself through the filters, the observer of men, the king of both gods and mortals.
From of old he has been the lord of riches; the Indu brings the well-sustained *ṛta* as something beautiful.
Like a courser hastening toward glory and gain, flow toward the feast of Indra and Vāyu.
As such, grant us thousands of great nourishments; O Soma, becoming pure, be the winner of wealth for us.
May the Soma juices, which invite the gods and are being poured out, flow toward our dwelling rich in heroic sons.
Like invokers who seek the sacrifice, they are the most delightful priests, possessing all boons and worthy of worship in heaven.
Thus, O God, flow for the sake of the divine host, O Soma, as a drink for the gods, for the great feast.
For we are indeed placed in the midst of great battle; O Purifier, set the two worlds, Heaven and Earth, in their firm positions.
Like a neighing horse harnessed with stallions, like a terrifying lion, he is swifter than thought. O Indu, flow toward us by the straightest paths; bring us benevolence.
A hundred streams, born of the gods, have been released; a thousand of these the seers cleanse.
O Indu, flow down from heaven as a winner of wealth; you are the leader of great riches.
Like the outpourings of heaven, the streams have been released through the days; like a wise king, he does not violate the covenant of Mitra.
Like a son following the wills of his father, flow for us toward this people’s freedom from harm.
Your honeyed streams have been poured forth as you, purified, pass through the sheep’s wool. O Pavamāna, you flow as the domain of the cows; being born, you have swollen the sun with your hymns.
Roaring along the path of Truth, you, the bright one, shine forth—the abode of Truth.
You flow for Indra as an exhilarating draught, sending forth your voice through the hymns of the sages.
O Soma, you, the divine bird of beautiful wings, look down from heaven, swelling your streams by your work at the banquet of the gods.
O Indu, enter the Soma-holding vessel; bellowing, go toward the ray of the sun.
The bearer sends forth three voices: the thought of *Ṛta*, the inspired wisdom of the sacred word (*brahman*).
Like cows seeking their lord, they go to him; like lowing thoughts, the prayers go toward Soma.
The milch-cows low longingly toward Soma; the sages, inquiring with their hymns, seek Soma.
The pressed Soma is purified as it is being anointed; the *arkas* and the *triṣṭubh* verses sing together in harmony to Soma.
Thus, O Soma, as you are being poured out and purified, flow for our well-being.
Enter Indra with a mighty roar; exalt our speech and generate abundance.
The watchful sage, the Soma being purified, has settled among the vessels through the thoughts of the sacred law.
Him the pairs of Adhvaryus, longing for him, serve—the charioteers with skillful hands.
Being purified, he has reached the sun as if from its source; he has filled both worlds and has illumined them.
He whose dear ones are indeed dear through his aid—may he grant us wealth by means of his song of praise.
Being purified, he is the increaser and the one who causes increase; may the bountiful Soma favor us with light.
By which means our ancient fathers, who knew the tracks and found the light, stole the cattle from the mountain.
The ocean roared in the first expanse, generating all creatures, the king of the world.
The bull Soma, the drop being pressed, has grown great upon the sheep’s-wool filter on its ridge.
Great indeed was that which Soma the buffalo performed, when as the embryo of the waters he chose the gods.
As Pavamāna, he bestowed vigor upon Indra; Indu generated light in the sun.
Being purified, exhilarate Vāyu for our desire and for wealth; exhilarate Mitra and Varuṇa.
Exhilarate the Marut host; exhilarate the gods; exhilarate Heaven and Earth, O divine Soma!
Flow straight on as the slayer of the crooked, driving away disease and our adversaries.
Blending your milk with the milk of the cows, you belong to Indra; we are your friends.
Flow pure as the distillation of honey, a fountain of wealth; flow to us for heroic sons and for good fortune.
O Indu, being purified, be sweet for Indra; flow to us with riches from the ocean.
Pressed out, Soma has flowed in a stream like a swift horse let loose; like a river to the lowlands, he has sped toward the prize.
Being purified, he has settled in his wooden seat; the vigorous one has flowed together with the milk and the waters.
This very Soma of yours, O Indra, flows for you in the vats—wise, powerful, and eager.
With sun-like vision, a charioteer, and true strength, he has been released like the longing of those who seek the gods.
Purifying himself with ancient vigor, assuming the forms of his daughter,
and clothing himself in a triple-layered protection within the waters, he goes singing like a priest to the assemblies.
Now, O divine Soma, as you are being purified, flow as a charioteer into the two bowls for us.
In the waters, he is most sweet, honeyed, and true to the *ṛta*, like the god Savitṛ whose thoughts are truth.
Flow toward Vāyu for his enjoyment while being praised; flow purified toward Mitra and Varuṇa.
Flow toward the hero who quickens the prayer and stands upon the chariot; flow toward Indra, the bull with the thunderbolt in his arm.
Flow toward us with well-woven garments; being purified, flow toward us with cows that yield milk easily.
O divine Soma, flow toward us with brilliant gold to be worn and with horses yoked to chariots.
Flow toward us, being purified, with celestial treasures and all earthly riches.
By which we may obtain wealth and flow toward us like Jamadagni, O Ṛṣi.
Flow with this purification toward these riches; O Indu, possessing all forms, run forth into the lake.
Even Bradhna, born like the wind, and Purumedhas shall give a hero to the swift one here.
And flow for us with these purifications, O Pavamāna, at the famous ford of Śravāyya. May Naiguta shake down sixty thousand treasures for our delight, like a ripe fruit from a tree.
Great indeed are his two names of virility, whether in the Māṃścatva or the Pṛśana, at the place of slaughter.
You sent the secret ones to sleep and made the enemies feel affection; you struck down the senseless one who was not to be cut down.
Seeking to pass through the three extended filters, you run toward one as you are being purified.
You are Bhaga; you are the giver of the gift; you are Maghavan, O Indu, for those who are liberal.
This wise Soma, the knower of all, flows as the king of the entire world;
sending forth his drops at the assemblies, Indu passes through the sheep’s wool filter and goes on his way.
The unerring buffaloes lick Indu; like eager poets, they sing at his station.
The wise urge him forward with ten fingers; they anoint his form with the essence of the waters.
O Soma, through you, the purifying one, may we continually win the prize in battle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
Flow toward us, O Indu, that wealth which best wins the prize, which is desired by many, which brings a thousandfold gain, which is full of great splendor, and which overcomes all powers.
Being pressed, he flows around.
The imperishable one has clothed himself in armor upon the chariot; Indu, urged on by the impulse, has flowed toward the fleece with his streams.
Being pressed, this Indu has flowed around the fleece, distilling exhilarating joy.
He whose streams rise upward at the sacrifice goes forth with brilliance, seeking cattle.
For you, O God, for every mortal who offers oblations, O Indu, you win wealth consisting of thousands and possessing a hundredfold life.
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Vasu, may we be the ones to receive from you this much-desired wealth;
O Adhrigu, may we be the very closest recipients of your nourishment and favor.
Him, the self-glorious one, whom the twenty sisters—struck by the pressing-stones—[have brought forth].
They cause the beloved, desirable, surging wave to overflow for Indra.
They purify him with the fleece— the lovely, golden-hued, brown one—
who goes to all the gods together with his exhilarating juice.
Through his protection, O you two who drink [the soma], he guards that which accomplishes skill;
he who among the patrons has established great renown, like the beloved sun in heaven.
At your sacrifices, O divine Heaven and Earth, this drop was born for the sake of Manu.
The god who dwells on the mountain, the goddess—O you of mighty roar, do not fail him!
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra to drink, for Vṛtra-slayer;
for the hero who bestows gifts, for the god who sits upon his seat.
Those ancient Soma-drops have flowed through the filter at the dawning of light—
driving away even the most crafty deceivers— at early morning, those lacking in wisdom.
O friends, you wise patrons and we ourselves [sing] that hymn which shines before us.
May we attain that which is fragrant with booty; may we win that which has a dwelling full of spoil.
For the beloved and bold one, they stretch out the bow as a manly deed; they weave bright garments for the Asura, seeking greatness at the forefront of inspired songs.

Then, adorned by the night, he plunges toward the spoils of war, when the prayers of Vivasvat urge the tawny steed to speed forth. We cleanse that exhilarating draught of his which is most beloved by Indra.

Whom the cows and the bulls established of old, and whom the wise poets establish now— him they have celebrated with an ancient song as he is being purified. And so the prayers, bearing the names of the gods, look toward him with longing.
They purify him, the sustainer, as he flows through the sheep’s wool filter;
the wise direct him like a messenger with their thoughts from of old.
Being purified, O Soma, most intoxicating, you settle within the vessels.

Like a bull depositing seed, he, the lord, is celebrated in our prayers; he, the god pressed for the gods, is cleansed by those of skillful deeds. When he finds his way into these [waters], he plunges into the great waters.
O Indu, pressed out and guided by the men, you are led through the filter; O most intoxicating one, you settle within the vessels for Indra.
The guileless ones sing toward him who is dear and beloved to Indra.

As mothers lick their calf born in the first age, so do they lick thee. O Indu, being purified, bring us, O Soma, doubly-increasing wealth; thou causest all treasures to flourish in the house of the donor.
Release the prayer yoked by the mind, as the thunder releases the rain; O Soma, you cause to flourish the treasures of the earth and those of heaven.
Your stream, once pressed, flows onward like that of a victorious warrior.
Rushing toward the sheep’s wool filter like a prize-winning steed,
O Soma, flow for us with your stream for wisdom and skill, O Sage;
you are pressed for Indra to drink, and for Mitra and Varuṇa as well.
Flow, O best winner of booty, pressed with your stream into the filter for Indra, for Viṣṇu, and for the gods— O Soma, you who are most rich in sweetness.
The guileless mothers lick you, the golden-hued one, in the filter.
Like cows toward their newborn calf, O Pavamāna, [the hymns flow] unto you in the supporting expanse. O Pavamāna, with your wondrous rays you go toward great renown;
boldly striking down the darkness, you dispel it all within the house of the donor.
O you of mighty vows, you have surpassed both heaven and earth; O Pavamāna, you have clothed yourself in your mantle by your own greatness.
For the conquest of you, the pressed juice, for the exhilarating draught—your strength.
Drive away the dog, O friends, the long-tongued one. He who, being pressed,
flows all around with a purifying stream—
the drop is like a horse that accomplishes its task.
The men, with all-encompassing thought, urge that Soma— which is difficult to win over— toward the sacrifice with the pressing-stones.
Pressed out, most rich in sweetness, the exhilarating Soma juices are for Indra.
Flowing forth with the purifying filter, may your exhilarating juices go to the gods.
"Indu flows for Indra," thus the gods have declared.
The Lord of Speech exerts himself as a sacrificer, ruling over all by his might.
In a thousand streams he flows, an ocean that stirs the voice; Soma, the lord of riches, the friend of Indra, day by day.
This Soma, being purified, flows as Pūṣan, as wealth, and as Bhaga.
The Lord of the entire world has looked out upon both heaven and earth.
Together the dear cows have lowed in joyful excitement for the exhilaration;
the Soma drops, as they are purified, prepare the paths.
O Pavamāna, bring us that which is most powerful and worthy of renown;
that wealth which surpasses the five tribes, by which we may conquer the forests. The Soma drops flow clear for us, they who best find the way.
The friends, being pressed, are stainless, well-disposed, and finders of the light.
Pressed out by the stones upon the ox-hide, they who are conscious and finders of wealth have raised their voices on every side for us, bestowing nourishment.
These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curds, are like the suns— beautiful to behold, moving swiftly, and firmly established in the clarified butter.
Like a mortal, one cannot restrain that speech of the flowing juice.
Drive away the dog that gives no gift, as the Bhr̥gus struck down Makha.
The kinsman has clothed himself in his mantle, like a son for enjoyment within the two arms of his parents.
He has gone forth like a lover to a maiden, like a bridegroom to sit upon the womb.
That hero, the accomplisher of skill, who has propped apart the two worlds—
he, the tawny one, has clothed himself in the filter, like a wise priest settling into his place.
Soma flows through the sheep’s woolly strainer upon the cowhide.
Neighing loudly, the tawny bull goes toward Indra’s appointed place;
the active infant of the great ones, impelling the vision of the sacred law (*ṛta*),
has encompassed all dear things— this is doubly so.
Near the two pressing-stones of Trita, that secret place which was shared; through the seven stations of the sacrifice, it is beloved.
With the stream of Trita, he has sent forth wealth upon the three ridges.
The one of excellent wisdom measures out his leagues.
As soon as he was born, the seven mothers instructed the wise one for the sake of glory.
He has become the steadfast lord of riches, since he has taken notice of this.
In his service, all the guileless gods are of one mind;
they become desirable delights when they take pleasure [in him]. He whom the upholders of *ṛta* have brought forth as a lovely embryo for all to see.
The sage, most bountiful, desired by many at the sacrifice—
the two great mothers of *Ṛta*, who move together toward him in person— when they, extending the sacrifice according to human custom, anoint him.
By his wisdom and with his bright guardians, he opened the stall of heaven; impelling the meditation of Truth at the sacrifice.
To Soma, the purifying ordainer, this exalted speech is offered.
I bring him offerings with my thoughts as if for his maintenance; may he take pleasure in them.
Anointed with the milk of cows, he flows through the sheep’s woolly filter. Being purified, the golden-hued one makes for himself three dwelling places.
He flows around the honey-dripping vat through the woolen filter;
the seven voices of the seers have sung aloud to him.
He, the leader of prayers, the one belonging to all gods, the undeceivable, flows around.
Soma, the tawny one, being purified, has entered the two bowls.
O immortal one, being purified by the priests along with the priests, go on the same chariot as Indra according to the divine ordinances.
Like a courser seeking the prize, the god, pressed for the gods, has flowed around. Pervading all, the purifying one rushes forth.
O friends, sit down; sing aloud to him who is being purified.
Adorn him for glory with sacrifices as if with a child;
let him loose together with his mothers like a calf, he who brings wealth to the household,
the exhilarating drink that wins the gods and possesses double strength.
Purify him who accomplishes skill, so that he may be for the feast of the host,
as one most auspicious for Mitra and Varuṇa. Singing voices have acclaimed you, the finder of wealth, for our sake.
With cows we clothe your hue;
O Indu, Lord of exhilarations, you are the celestial nymph for the gods. Like a friend to a friend, be the best finder of the path.
Drive far away from us every demon and every devouring fiend;
ward off from us the godless and the double-tongued oppressor.
O friends, sing forth to him who is being purified for your exhilaration.
They sweeten him with sacrifices and hymns of praise, as one would a child;
like a calf with its mothers, Indu, being urged forward, is anointed, he who favors the gods, adorned by our exhilarating prayers.
This is the means for accomplishing skill; this is for the feast of the host. This most honey-sweet juice has been pressed for the gods.
O Indu, flow with power, being pressed like one rich in cattle and horses. Flow, O most skillful one!
I have established your bright color within the cows. O Indu,
lord of the tawny steeds, most excellent as a divine feast for the gods,
be like a friend to a friend, a hero for our glory.
Drive far away from us every devouring demon, O God; overcoming the adversaries, O Indu, cast away the double-dealer.
May these pressed juices go toward Indra, the bull, with their golden hues.
Born through obedience, the drops have found the light of heaven.
This pressed juice flows for Indra, bringing gain for the battle; Soma takes heed of victory, as he knows how.
In the exhilarations of this [Soma], may Indra grasp the prize-winning handle;
and let him, the winner of waters, wield the bull-like thunderbolt.
O Soma, flow forth, thou who art watchful; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Bring hither brilliant, light-winning vigor; flow for Indra as a bull-like exhilarating draught, O thou who art visible to all.
Maker of paths with a thousand courses, look forth upon the world.
Best finder of the path for us, most honey-sweet for the gods,
go forth by a thousand paths with a loud roar. Flow on with your streams in might, O Indu, for the feast of the gods.
O honeyed Soma, sit within our vessel. Your drops, floating upon the water, have strengthened Indra for exhilaration;
the immortal gods have drunk you for the sake of immortality.
O pressed drops of Soma, as you are purified, flow hither to us with wealth—
ye who cause rain to fall, who are lords of the earth, and who find the light of heaven.
Purifying himself with his wave, Soma flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
Pavamāna, bellowing at the forefront of speech,
they urge the prize-winning steed with their prayers as he sports in the wood, passing through the sheep’s fleece;
the hymns have sounded together toward him whose back is tripled.
He has been let loose toward the jars like a prize-seeking steed in the contest; purifying himself and generating speech, he has flowed forth.
The beloved, golden-hued one flows with speed through the winding channels.
Flow toward the singers with glory consisting of heroic sons.
Flow on thus, seeking the gods; streams of honey have been released. Chanting, you pass through the filter from every side.
Pour out on every side the pressed juice, the Soma which is the highest oblation.
He who, the friend of men, has flowed through the waters, has pressed the Soma with the stones.
Now, being purified by the sheep’s wool, flow around—unassailable and most fragrant.
When you are pressed, we rejoice in you with the juice even in the waters, blending you, the supreme one, with the milk of cows.
Being pressed for all to see, the exhilarating god, Indu, the far-seeing power of the mind, flows forth.
O Soma, being purified, you flow in a stream, clothing yourself in the waters.
Bringing treasures, you sit upon the womb of Truth; O God, you are a golden fountain.
Milking the heavenly udder for the dear honey, he has taken his seat in the ancient dwelling-place.
The prize-winning one flows toward the support that must be sought; shaken by men, he, the far-seeing, pours forth.
Being purified, O Soma, the watchful one, you flow through the sheep’s wool, dear to all.
You have become a sage, the best of the Aṅgirases; sprinkle our sacrifice with honey.
Soma, the bounteous, flows on, the finder of the path, the seer, the inspired singer, the far-seeing.
You became a seer, the one most beloved by the gods; you caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Pressed by the pressers, O Soma, upon the backs of the sheep’s wool, you flow like a bay horse with your stream; you flow with a gladdening stream.
In the watery place, Soma, rich in cattle, has been guarded with cattle; he has been guarded with milked cows.
Like the ocean, they have gone to the enclosures; exhilarating, he flows for intoxication.
Pressed by the stones, O Soma, you flow through the sheep’s wool filter.
Like a person entering a city, the tawny one has entered the two bowls; you have taken your seat within the wooden vessels.
He has cleansed himself through the fine wool of the sheep, like a prize-winning steed eager for the contest at the sacrifice.
Soma Pavamāna is to be celebrated by the wise, by the inspired singers and the chanters of hymns.
O Soma, for the banquet of the gods, you have swelled like a river with its flood; you are the exhilarating stalk, watchful as one who awakens, flowing toward the honey-dripping vat.
The beloved one has clothed himself in a bright garment, like a son to be adorned by his father. The skillful workers urge him forth from both hands into the rivers, as one drives a chariot.
The Soma-drops, the active ones, flow toward the intoxicating exhilaration;
upon the surface of the ocean, they are wise, exhilarating, and finders of heaven.
Crossing over the ocean with his wave, the purifying King, the god, [fulfills] the lofty cosmic order.
Flowing according to the law of Mitra and Varuṇa, being urged forward, he promotes the lofty *ṛta*. Guided by men, desirable, far-seeing, the King, the God of the ocean.
The exhilarating Soma, pressed for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, flows clear.
Flowing in a thousand streams, he speeds across the sheep’s wool; him the Āyus purify. Being purified in the ladle, generating the hymn, the Seer Soma rejoices among the gods.
Clothed in waters, superior with the products of the cow, he has settled within the wooden vats.

O Soma, O Indu, day after day I have rejoiced in thy friendship. O tawny one, many things come toward me; protect me, pass beyond those barriers. And I, O tawny Soma, am at thy breast by night and by day for the sake of thy friendship.
Beyond the sun that burns with heat, we have flown away like birds.
Being cleansed by the skillful hand, you send forth your voice in the ocean.
O Pavamāna, you flow toward us with wealth that is tawny, abundant, and much-desired.
Being cleansed in the sheep’s wool filter, O Pavamāna, the bull has bellowed in the wood.
O Soma, being purified, you flow toward the appointed place of the gods, adorned with milk. Flow on for the winning of booty, toward all poetic wisdoms.
O exhilarating Soma, you were the first to spread out the ocean for the gods. Flow on, O Soma, around the earthly realm and the celestial realms according to your laws.
O far-seeing one, the sages urge you on with their prayers and meditations—you, the radiant one.
The purifying drops have been released in a stream across the filter;
accompanied by the Maruts, exhilarating, and impetuous like Indra’s horses, they flow toward wisdom and sacrificial foods.
Clothed in waters, the drop, urged on by the pressers, hastens around the vat.
Generating light, he has made the lowing cows low, as if preparing a garment for himself.
Flow on, O Soma, most rich in sweetness, the best provider of wisdom, the exhilarating draught for Indra;
flow as the great, most celestial exhilaration.

Having drunk of whom the bull acts like a bull, he who finds the light— he, the one with excellent awareness, has stepped forth toward the quarters, like Etaśa toward the prize. For you indeed, O most brilliant Pavamāna, [have surpassed] the divine generations.
You have proclaimed for the sake of immortality—
that [soma] by which Navagva opened the two doors, by which the sages attained their desire,
and by which they reached glorious fame within the favor of the gods and the lovely nectar of immortality.
This very one, pressed out, flows in a stream through the sheep’s woolly filter as the most intoxicating draught;
he plays like a wave of waters.
He who by his might cleft the kine from within the rock, the cows that belong to the dawn and the waters.
You have extended that which you approach—the wealth of cattle and horses; O bold one, break it open like a warrior clad in armor.
Press out and pour forth the praise-song for him who is like a horse, the overcomer of waters, the traverser of the mid-air, the one who climbs the tree and floats upon the waters.
The bull with a thousand streams, the increaser of milk, dear to the divine race—
He who, born of *ṛta*, has grown great by *ṛta*, the King, the God, the lofty *ṛta*. O Lord of food,
shine forth with lofty splendor and glory, O God who loves the gods!
Unsheath yourself from the middle [vessel]; O most skillful one, flow toward us, pressed into the two bowls like a lord of the people who is the bearer of the clans.
Flow as the rain from heaven, as the stream of waters; quicken our prayers for the sake of winning cattle.
They have milked from heaven that bull, distilling exhilaration, with a thousand streams, who bears all treasures within him.
The immortal bull was born, engendering [life] and dispelling the darkness with his light.

Well-praised by the seers, he has assumed his radiant garment through his triple power and wondrous deed. He is pressed— the one who brings wealth, who brings riches, who brings the *iḷā*-offerings, Soma, who brings secure dwellings.
Of whomsoever Indra shall drink, of whomsoever the Maruts, or Bhaga along with Aryaman;
by whom we may bring Mitra and Varuṇa hither, and Indra for our great protection—
O Soma, most intoxicating, well-armed, and prepared by the men, flow for Indra to drink.
Flow on, most rich in honey!
Enter the heart of Indra, the receptacle of Soma, as rivers flow into the ocean—
pleasing to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the highest pillar of heaven.
Flow forth, O Soma, as a sweet draught for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, and for Bhaga.

O Soma, may Indra drink of thee when thou art pressed, for the sake of wisdom and skill, and for all the gods. Thus flow, as the bright celestial nectar, for the sake of immortality and the great dwelling.
Flow on, O Soma, as a great ocean, the father of the gods, toward all abodes. Flow clear for the gods, O Soma, for heaven and earth, and for the welfare of all creatures.
You are the sustainer of heaven, the bright nectar; flow as a prize-winning steed within the realm of truth.

Flow on, O Soma, radiant and with a fine stream, as the ancient one through the great sheep’s fleece. Guided by men, born and purified, may the exhilarating one who finds the light flow forth, bestowing all things. Indu, being purified and choosing progeny, shall create for us all riches.
Flow on, O Soma, for wisdom and skill, like a groomed courser for the prize of wealth.
The pressers purify that juice of yours, the Soma, for exhilaration and for great splendor.
They cleanse the infant, the tawny drop, the Soma, at his birth, in the filter for the gods.
The lovely drop has flowed for exhilaration, a sage in the lap of the waters, for the sake of fortune.
He bears the lovely name of Indra, by which he struck down all the Vṛtras.
All the gods drink of this, when it is mixed with milk and pressed by men.
Pressed out, he has flowed forth in a thousand streams across the filter, through the sheep’s woolly fleece.
That vigorous steed, with a thousandfold seed, being cleansed by the waters and mixed with milk.
O Soma, go forward into the belly of Indra, guided by the men and pressed by the stones.
The prize-winning steed, Soma, has been released through the filter in a thousand streams for Indra.
They anoint him, the drop, with the essence of honey, for the sake of exhilaration, for Indra the bull.
For the gods, they cleanse you, the tawny one, who clothe yourself in the waters, so that you may display your vigor at will.
The drop flows for Indra; it flows down, the fierce one, mixing itself as it releases the waters.
Flow forth well for the winning of booty, you who overcome all obstacles.
Crossing over our enemies, you go like a collector of debts.
For we rejoice after thee, O Soma, when thou art pressed, in the great sovereignty over the battle.
O Pavamāna, thou plungest forward toward the spoils of war. For thou, O Pavamāna, by thy power hast generated the sun and the milk for its support.
Rushing with the cow-swift *purandhi*, he has generated the immortal among mortals, according to the ordinance of *ṛta* and the lovely nectar. Ever-flowing, he hastens toward the prize of booty.
For you have pierced through with glory, like an inexhaustible spring for the people’s drinking;
bearing [the prize] in your hands as if with arrows,
some, beholding this kinship, have sung forth in praise, shining with wealth toward the heavens.
Like Savitar, the god, he unrolls the veil.
In thee, O Soma, those who have spread the sacrificial grass first fixed their thoughts upon great strength and glory.
As such, O hero, impel us toward heroic power.
The ancient nectar of heaven, worthy of praise, he milked forth from the great depth of the sky;
they raised their voices together toward Indra as he was being born.
And now, O Pavamāna, when you [fill] these two worlds, heaven and earth, and all these beings with your might.
Like a bull standing at the head of the herd, you spread yourself abroad.
Soma, being purified in the sheep’s wool, flows as he purifies himself, like a child playing;
the drop has a thousand streams and possesses a hundredfold vigor.
This Indu, being purified, flows as a sweet wave for Indra, rich in honey, faithful to the Law (ṛta), the winner of booty, the finder of wide space,
and the bestower of vital strength. Flow on, O conqueror of those who attack us, driving away the demons and clearing the paths of distress.

Well-armed and victorious over his enemies, O Soma, with this golden luster while being purified, he overcomes all hostilities with his self-yoked steeds, like the sun with his self-yoked steeds. The stream of the pressed juice shines as he is purified, the ruddy, golden-hued one;
when he encompasses all forms with the chanters, with the seven-mouthed chanters.

You found that treasure of the Paṇis; you cleanse yourself with your mothers in your own home by means of the inspirations of Truth, in your home. Like [a song] from afar, that melody arises where the prayers resound. With his threefold red rays he has assumed vital strength;

shining, he has assumed vital strength. He goes along the eastern direction, observing keenly; the beautiful chariot strives with its reins, the divine, beautiful chariot. The hymns of manly power have come forth for Indra’s victory.
And when you two become the unshakable thunderbolt, unshakable in battles;

for our thoughts are indeed diverse, as are the religious observances of men—the carpenter seeks what is broken, the physician seeks the sick, and the priest seeks one who presses the Soma; O Indu, flow forth for Indra!
With aging plants and with the feathers of birds,
the smith, seeking with stones and bellows one rich in gold, O Indu, flow around for Indra.
I am a poet, my father is a physician, and my mother is a grinder of stones.
Desiring wealth with various thoughts, we follow thee like cattle; O Indu, flow for Indra.
The horse is the drawer of the easy-gliding chariot; the lover seeks his laughing mistress;
the phallus desires the hairy testicles; the frog seeks the water; O Indu, flow for Indra.
Let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma at Śaryaṇāvat;
bestowing strength upon himself, performing great heroic deeds—O Indu, flow around for Indra!
Flow hither, O Lord of the quarters, O bounteous Soma from Ārjīka!
Pressed by the word of Truth, by sincerity, by faith, and by austerity—O Indu, flow around for Indra.
The Daughter of the Sun brought that bull, who had grown strong through Parjanya.
The Gandharvas received him; they placed that essence in the Soma. O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Speaking the *ṛta*, O you whose splendor is *ṛta*; speaking the truth, O you whose deeds are truth;
speaking with faith, O King Soma, you who are adorned by the Creator—O Indu, flow forth for Indra!
The outpourings of the mighty, vast, and true one flow together.
The flavorful juices come together as you are purified by the sacred word, O tawny one; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where the Brahmā priest, O Pavamāna, speaking rhythmic speech, exalts with the pressing-stone at the Soma—generating bliss through the Soma—flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where there is eternal light, in that world where the sun is established—there place me, O Pavamāna, in the immortal, imperishable world;
flow around for Indra, O Indu! Where King Vaivasvata dwells, where the gate of heaven is located—there place me, O Pavamāna, in the immortal, imperishable world; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where those waters flow unceasingly, there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Where one may roam at will in the triple vault, the third heaven of the sky, where the worlds are full of light—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Where desires and longings are fulfilled, where is the summit of the sun; where self-sustenance and satisfaction abide—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow for Indra!
Where joys and delights, pleasures and gladnesses dwell.
Where the desires of desire are attained, there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
He who has stepped into the domains of the purifying Indu—him they call one of noble progeny, he who, O Soma, has won your mind; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
O Sage Kaśyapa, among the seers who compose the mantras, magnify our songs with your hymns.
Pay homage to King Soma, who was born as the lord of plants; O Indu, flow forth for Indra. The seven directions have their various suns; there are seven officiating priests, the *hotṛ*s.
O Soma, with those seven Āditya gods, protect us! O Indu, flow around for Indra.
O King, with that oblation of yours which has been cooked, protect us, O Soma!
Let not the hostile one overcome us, nor let anything afflict us; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
